spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od0m7p2t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Suites, Machines, MaxRecount, IDLE

\* store: machines parked centrally; fitted: machines in each suite.
\* moving: the one transfer in progress, carrying the tally it recorded.
\* tally: each suite's compare-and-swap equipment register.
VARIABLES store, fitted, moving, tally

vars == <<store, fitted, moving, tally>>

Transfers == [to: Suites, amt: 1..Machines, seen: 0..MaxRecount]

TypeOK ==
    /\ store \in 0..Machines
    /\ fitted \in [Suites -> 0..Machines]
    /\ moving \in Transfers \cup {IDLE}
    /\ tally \in [Suites -> 0..MaxRecount]

Init ==
    /\ store = Machines
    /\ fitted = [s \in Suites |-> 0]
    /\ moving = IDLE
    /\ tally = [s \in Suites |-> 0]

Fittedtotal ==
    LET add[S \in SUBSET Suites] ==
        IF S = {} THEN 0
        ELSE LET s == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE IN fitted[s] + add[S \ {s}]
    IN add[Suites]

InTransit == IF moving = IDLE THEN 0 ELSE moving.amt

\* The store is debited when the trolleys leave, not when they arrive.
Dispatch(s, n) ==
    /\ moving = IDLE
    /\ n <= store
    /\ store' = store - n
    /\ moving' = [to |-> s, amt |-> n, seen |-> tally[s]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fitted, tally>>

Book ==
    /\ moving # IDLE
    /\ tally[moving.to] = moving.seen
    /\ fitted' = [fitted EXCEPT ![moving.to] = @ + moving.amt]
    /\ moving' = IDLE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<store, tally>>

\* A refused transfer goes back whole; machines are never split in transit.
Refuse ==
    /\ moving # IDLE
    /\ tally[moving.to] # moving.seen
    /\ store' = store + moving.amt
    /\ moving' = IDLE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fitted, tally>>

Send(s, n) ==
    /\ n > 0
    /\ n <= fitted[s]
    /\ fitted' = [fitted EXCEPT ![s] = @ - n]
    /\ store' = store + n
    /\ UNCHANGED <<moving, tally>>

Recount(s) ==
    /\ tally[s] < MaxRecount
    /\ tally' = [tally EXCEPT ![s] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<store, fitted, moving>>

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Suites, n \in 1..Machines : Dispatch(s, n) \/ Send(s, n)
    \/ Book \/ Refuse
    \/ \E s \in Suites : Recount(s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(Book) /\ WF_vars(Refuse)

MachinesAreConserved == store + Fittedtotal + InTransit = Machines

NoTransferStaysInTransit == (moving # IDLE) ~> (moving = IDLE)
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Suites = {mainBlock, daySurgery}
    Machines = 2
    MaxRecount = 2
    IDLE = IDLE

INVARIANT MachinesAreConserved

PROPERTY NoTransferStaysInTransit
nl:
A hospital runs two operating-room suites that schedule independently of one another: the main theatre block and the day-surgery block. They share one central store of anaesthetic machines. A machine is a physical trolley, so at any instant every machine the hospital owns is in exactly one of three places — parked in the central store, fitted in one of the two suites, or on a porter's trolley being wheeled between them. Machines are neither built nor scrapped during the day.

Because the two suites do not talk to each other, transfers are serialised through the store: only one transfer is in progress at a time. The store debits itself the moment a transfer starts, when the machines physically leave the store room, rather than when they arrive — a machine in a corridor is not available to be promised to the other suite.

Each suite keeps a small compare-and-swap tally register recording its own equipment count, and the register changes whenever the suite recounts. A transfer records the value of the destination suite's register as it stood when the transfer started. On arrival the porter compares: if the destination's register still holds the value the transfer recorded, the machines are booked into that suite and the transfer is done. If the suite has recounted in the meantime, the arrival paperwork no longer matches the suite's books, so the transfer is refused and the machines go straight back into the central store — whole, never split. Suites also send machines back to the store directly when a list finishes, which needs no paperwork.

The full set of actions is: Dispatch, in which the store debits some machines and starts a transfer to a suite, recording that suite's current tally register; Book, in which an arriving transfer whose recorded tally still matches the destination suite is booked into that suite's fitted equipment and closed; Refuse, in which an arriving transfer whose recorded tally no longer matches is closed and its machines returned whole to the store; Send, in which a suite returns some of its fitted machines to the store directly; and Recount, in which a suite recounts its equipment, advancing its tally register and so invalidating any transfer already on its way.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The machines parked in the central store, plus those fitted across both suites, plus those on the transfer in progress, always add up to exactly the number of machines the hospital owns.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: No transfer is left in the corridor forever — every transfer that is dispatched is eventually closed, either booked into its suite or refused back to the store.

---- MODULE W4Od6m9p2t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Cars, ContractHours, MaxEpoch

\* duty: hours assigned to each car; reserve: hours not yet handed out.
\* epoch: the traffic profile in force; draining: cars are giving hours back.
VARIABLES duty, reserve, epoch, draining

vars == <<duty, reserve, epoch, draining>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ duty \in [Cars -> 0..ContractHours]
    /\ reserve \in 0..ContractHours
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ draining \in BOOLEAN

Init ==
    /\ duty = [c \in Cars |-> 0]
    /\ reserve = ContractHours
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ draining = FALSE

Assigned ==
    LET add[S \in SUBSET Cars] ==
        IF S = {} THEN 0
        ELSE LET c == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE IN duty[c] + add[S \ {c}]
    IN add[Cars]

OpenEpoch ==
    /\ ~draining
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ draining' = TRUE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<duty, reserve>>

Drain(c, n) ==
    /\ draining
    /\ n <= duty[c]
    /\ duty' = [duty EXCEPT ![c] = @ - n]
    /\ reserve' = reserve + n
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, draining>>

CloseEpoch ==
    /\ draining
    /\ \A c \in Cars : duty[c] = 0
    /\ draining' = FALSE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<duty, reserve, epoch>>

\* Hours are handed out only outside a reconfiguration.
Assign(c, n) ==
    /\ ~draining
    /\ n <= reserve
    /\ reserve' = reserve - n
    /\ duty' = [duty EXCEPT ![c] = @ + n]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, draining>>

\* The manager does not queue behind the epoch machinery, but moves hours
\* a car actually holds; the contract total is not the manager's to change.
Override(c, d, n) ==
    /\ c # d
    /\ n > 0
    /\ n <= duty[c]
    /\ duty' = [duty EXCEPT ![c] = @ - n, ![d] = @ + n]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reserve, epoch, draining>>

Next ==
    \/ OpenEpoch \/ CloseEpoch
    \/ \E c \in Cars, n \in 1..ContractHours : Drain(c, n) \/ Assign(c, n)
    \/ \E c, d \in Cars : \E n \in 1..ContractHours : Override(c, d, n)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

ContractHoursAreConserved == reserve + Assigned = ContractHours
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Cars = {carA, carB, carC}
    ContractHours = 4
    MaxEpoch = 2

INVARIANT ContractHoursAreConserved
nl:
A skyscraper's elevator bank allocates duty hours to its cars. The building's lift-service contract buys a fixed number of duty hours per day, and those hours are the quantity the bank has to account for: an hour is either assigned to a specific car or sitting unassigned in the bank's reserve. Hours are not created during the day and none are thrown away — every hour the contract bought is somewhere.

The bank's traffic profile is reconfigured under an epoch number as the day changes shape: morning up-peak, midday interfloor, evening down-peak. A reconfiguration is not a single instantaneous rewrite of the allocation. Opening a new epoch puts the bank into draining mode, and while draining, cars give their assigned hours back to the reserve, a car at a time, until every car is at zero; only then does the reconfiguration close and the bank leave draining mode. Hours are handed out to cars again from the reserve once draining has finished, so a car is never being drained and topped up at the same time.

The building manager has a privileged override. During a stuck lift, a VIP move, or a fire drill the manager moves duty hours from one car to another directly, without waiting for the epoch machinery and without regard to whether the bank is draining. That is the point of the override: it does not queue behind a reconfiguration. It does not, however, mint hours. The manager can only move hours a car actually has, and the hours land on the other car; the contract total is not something the manager can change.

The full set of actions is: OpenEpoch, in which the bank advances to the next traffic epoch and enters draining mode; Drain, in which a car in draining mode gives some of its assigned hours back to the reserve; CloseEpoch, in which draining mode ends once every car is at zero assigned hours; Assign, in which the bank hands hours out of the reserve to a car while not draining; and Override, in which the manager moves hours directly from one car to another at any time.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The hours sitting in the bank's reserve, plus the hours assigned across all the cars, always add up to exactly the number of duty hours the service contract bought.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od10m9p6t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Controllers, Points, MaxEra, NONE

\* vested: which controller may drive each point; era: the control epoch,
\* advanced on every vesting change. bus: commands in flight, unordered.
\* standing: the command each point machine last acted on.
VARIABLES vested, era, bus, standing

vars == <<vested, era, bus, standing>>

Commands == [by: Controllers, point: Points, era: 0..MaxEra]
Standings == [by: Controllers, era: 0..MaxEra]

TypeOK ==
    /\ vested \in [Points -> Controllers \cup {NONE}]
    /\ era \in [Points -> 0..MaxEra]
    /\ bus \subseteq Commands
    /\ standing \in [Points -> Standings \cup {NONE}]

Init ==
    /\ vested = [p \in Points |-> NONE]
    /\ era = [p \in Points |-> 0]
    /\ bus = {}
    /\ standing = [p \in Points |-> NONE]

Vest(c, p) ==
    /\ vested[p] = NONE
    /\ era[p] < MaxEra
    /\ vested' = [vested EXCEPT ![p] = c]
    /\ era' = [era EXCEPT ![p] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bus, standing>>

Send(c, p) ==
    /\ vested[p] = c
    /\ ~(\E m \in bus : m.by = c /\ m.point = p)
    /\ bus' = bus \cup {[by |-> c, point |-> p, era |-> era[p]]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<vested, era, standing>>

\* Acted on only at the epoch it was sent under, and only for its sender.
Act(m) ==
    /\ m \in bus
    /\ era[m.point] = m.era
    /\ vested[m.point] = m.by
    /\ standing' = [standing EXCEPT ![m.point] = [by |-> m.by, era |-> m.era]]
    /\ bus' = bus \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<vested, era>>

Drop(m) ==
    /\ m \in bus
    /\ \/ era[m.point] # m.era
       \/ vested[m.point] # m.by
    /\ bus' = bus \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<vested, era, standing>>

Release(p) ==
    /\ vested[p] # NONE
    /\ era[p] < MaxEra
    /\ vested' = [vested EXCEPT ![p] = NONE]
    /\ era' = [era EXCEPT ![p] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bus, standing>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Controllers, p \in Points : Vest(c, p) \/ Send(c, p)
    \/ \E m \in Commands : Act(m) \/ Drop(m)
    \/ \E p \in Points : Release(p)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
        /\ \A m \in Commands : WF_vars(Act(m)) /\ WF_vars(Drop(m))

StandingCommandIsAuthorised ==
    \A p \in Points :
        (standing[p] # NONE /\ standing[p].era = era[p])
            => vested[p] = standing[p].by

NoCommandSitsOnTheBus ==
    \A m \in Commands : (m \in bus) ~> (m \notin bus)
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Controllers = {ctlA, ctlB}
    Points = {pt101, pt102}
    MaxEra = 1
    NONE = NONE

INVARIANT StandingCommandIsAuthorised

PROPERTY NoCommandSitsOnTheBus
nl:
A subway signalling system drives its point machines from a control centre, but which controller is allowed to drive a given point is not fixed. Areas of the railway are vested in controllers and re-vested as shifts change, as a possession is taken for engineering work, or as a fault forces a hand-back. Every change of vesting — taking an area, and giving it up — advances that point's control epoch, and the epoch is what tells a stale command from a current one.

Commands do not reach the point machines in the order they were sent. They go onto an unordered command bus and are picked up in whatever order the bus manages, so a command sent under an old vesting can easily arrive after the area has been re-vested to somebody else. Each command carries the controller that sent it, the point it addresses, and the control epoch that was in force when it was sent. A controller has at most one command outstanding per point.

A point machine acts on a command only when the command's epoch still matches the point's current epoch and the point is still vested in the controller that sent it. When it acts, it records the command as the standing command for that point, keeping both the sending controller and the epoch. A command that fails either check is not acted on and is dropped off the bus.

The full set of actions is: Vest, in which an unvested point is vested in a controller, advancing its epoch; Send, in which the controller a point is vested in puts a command for that point onto the bus, stamped with the point's current epoch, provided it has none outstanding for that point; Act, in which a point machine takes a command off the bus whose epoch still matches and whose sender is still the vested controller, and records it as the point's standing command; Drop, in which a command whose epoch is stale or whose sender no longer holds the vesting is taken off the bus unacted; and Release, in which a point's vesting is given up, advancing its epoch.

SAFETY PROPERTY: If a point's standing command still carries that point's current control epoch, then the controller that sent it is still the controller the point is vested in, so no point is left acting on a command from an unauthorised or superseded controller.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: No command sits on the bus forever — every command put onto the bus is eventually taken off it, either acted on or dropped.

---- MODULE W4Od8m5p4t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Students, Nodes, Cap, Quorum, NONE

\* admitted: students in the section; open: the one proposal under vote,
\* which holds a promised seat; tally: nodes that have voted on it.
VARIABLES admitted, open, tally, withdrawn

vars == <<admitted, open, tally, withdrawn>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ admitted \subseteq Students
    /\ open \in Students \cup {NONE}
    /\ tally \subseteq Nodes
    /\ withdrawn \subseteq Students

Init ==
    /\ admitted = {}
    /\ open = NONE
    /\ tally = {}
    /\ withdrawn = {}

\* A promised seat counts against the cap from the instant it is promised.
Promised == IF open = NONE THEN 0 ELSE 1
Occupied == Cardinality(admitted)

Propose(s) ==
    /\ open = NONE
    /\ s \notin admitted
    /\ Occupied + 1 <= Cap
    /\ open' = s
    /\ tally' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<admitted, withdrawn>>

Vote(n) ==
    /\ open # NONE
    /\ n \notin tally
    /\ tally' = tally \cup {n}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<admitted, open, withdrawn>>

Admit ==
    /\ open # NONE
    /\ Cardinality(tally) >= Quorum
    /\ admitted' = admitted \cup {open}
    /\ open' = NONE
    /\ tally' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED withdrawn

Withdraw ==
    /\ open # NONE
    /\ Cardinality(tally) < Quorum
    /\ open' = NONE
    /\ tally' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<admitted, withdrawn>>

\* The dean skips the vote, never the fire officer's count.
Override(s) ==
    /\ s \notin admitted
    /\ s # open
    /\ Occupied + Promised + 1 <= Cap
    /\ admitted' = admitted \cup {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<open, tally, withdrawn>>

Drop(s) ==
    /\ s \in admitted
    /\ admitted' = admitted \ {s}
    /\ withdrawn' = withdrawn \cup {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<open, tally>>

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Students : Propose(s) \/ Override(s) \/ Drop(s)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Vote(n)
    \/ Admit \/ Withdraw

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

WithinFireCap == Occupied + Promised <= Cap
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Students = {sIvy, sJun, sKai}
    Nodes = {regA, regB, regC}
    Cap = 2
    Quorum = 2
    NONE = NONE

INVARIANT WithinFireCap
nl:
A university course-registration system admits students to a laboratory section whose size is capped by the fire officer, not by the department. The cap is a hard number of bodies in the room and nothing in the registration system is allowed to exceed it.

Admissions are not made by any single registrar node. An admission is opened as a proposal naming one student, and the proposal takes a seat out of the room's allowance the moment it is opened, before any node has voted — a seat that has been promised to a proposal cannot also be offered to somebody else while the vote runs. Only one proposal is open at a time. Registrar nodes then vote on the open proposal one at a time, and once a quorum of them has voted the student is admitted and the proposal closes, converting the promised seat into an occupied one. A proposal that has not reached quorum can be closed unmade instead, and its promised seat goes back into the allowance.

The dean has a privileged override and can admit a student directly with no vote at all. That is the point of the override: it does not wait for the registrar nodes and it does not queue behind an open proposal. What the dean cannot do is put a body in the room that the fire officer has not allowed for, so the dean's admission counts the students already admitted and any seat currently promised to an open proposal, and only goes ahead if there is still room after both.

Students also leave. A student who has been admitted may withdraw from the section, which frees the seat and puts the student on the withdrawn list; the seat is then available again.

The full set of actions is: Propose, in which a proposal is opened for a student who is not already admitted, taking a seat from the allowance and clearing the vote tally; Vote, in which one registrar node that has not yet voted votes on the open proposal; Admit, in which a proposal that has reached quorum admits its student and closes; Withdraw, in which a proposal that has not reached quorum is closed unmade and its promised seat released; Override, in which the dean admits a student directly, provided the students already admitted plus any seat promised to an open proposal still leave room under the cap; and Drop, in which an admitted student leaves the section and is recorded as withdrawn.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of students admitted to the section, counted together with the seat promised to an open proposal if there is one, never exceeds the cap the fire officer set.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od17m7p6t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Handlers, Chutes, MaxVersion, NONE

\* version: each chute's compare-and-swap register, advanced on every
\* ownership change. owner: who may drive the chute. prepared: the command a
\* slow handler is carrying. standing: the divert the chute is running.
VARIABLES version, owner, prepared, standing

vars == <<version, owner, prepared, standing>>

Drafts == [chute: Chutes, version: 0..MaxVersion]
Diverts == [by: Handlers, version: 0..MaxVersion]

TypeOK ==
    /\ version \in [Chutes -> 0..MaxVersion]
    /\ owner \in [Chutes -> Handlers \cup {NONE}]
    /\ prepared \in [Handlers -> Drafts \cup {NONE}]
    /\ standing \in [Chutes -> Diverts \cup {NONE}]

Init ==
    /\ version = [c \in Chutes |-> 0]
    /\ owner = [c \in Chutes |-> NONE]
    /\ prepared = [h \in Handlers |-> NONE]
    /\ standing = [c \in Chutes |-> NONE]

Take(h, c) ==
    /\ owner[c] = NONE
    /\ version[c] < MaxVersion
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![c] = h]
    /\ version' = [version EXCEPT ![c] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<prepared, standing>>

Prepare(h, c) ==
    /\ owner[c] = h
    /\ prepared[h] = NONE
    /\ prepared' = [prepared EXCEPT ![h] = [chute |-> c, version |-> version[c]]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, owner, standing>>

\* The controller re-checks at commit time, because the handler is slow.
Commit(h) ==
    /\ prepared[h] # NONE
    /\ version[prepared[h].chute] = prepared[h].version
    /\ owner[prepared[h].chute] = h
    /\ standing' = [standing EXCEPT ![prepared[h].chute] =
                        [by |-> h, version |-> prepared[h].version]]
    /\ prepared' = [prepared EXCEPT ![h] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, owner>>

Void(h) ==
    /\ prepared[h] # NONE
    /\ \/ version[prepared[h].chute] # prepared[h].version
       \/ owner[prepared[h].chute] # h
    /\ prepared' = [prepared EXCEPT ![h] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, owner, standing>>

Hand(c) ==
    /\ owner[c] # NONE
    /\ version[c] < MaxVersion
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![c] = NONE]
    /\ version' = [version EXCEPT ![c] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<prepared, standing>>

\* Every chute has used up its version register and nothing is prepared:
\* the sortation run is over and the router idles.
Idle ==
    /\ \A c \in Chutes : version[c] = MaxVersion
    /\ \A h \in Handlers : prepared[h] = NONE
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E h \in Handlers, c \in Chutes : Take(h, c) \/ Prepare(h, c)
    \/ \E h \in Handlers : Commit(h) \/ Void(h)
    \/ \E c \in Chutes : Hand(c)
    \/ Idle

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
        /\ \A h \in Handlers : WF_vars(Commit(h)) /\ WF_vars(Void(h))

Live == {c \in Chutes : standing[c] # NONE /\ standing[c].version = version[c]}

StandingDivertsAreOwned ==
    {<<c, standing[c].by>> : c \in Live} \subseteq {<<c, owner[c]>> : c \in Chutes}

NoPreparedCommandLingers ==
    \A h \in Handlers : (prepared[h] # NONE) ~> (prepared[h] = NONE)
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Handlers = {hOne, hTwo}
    Chutes = {chuteA, chuteB}
    MaxVersion = 2
    NONE = NONE

INVARIANT StandingDivertsAreOwned

PROPERTY NoPreparedCommandLingers
nl:
An airport baggage router sorts bags onto chutes. Each chute is driven by whichever sortation handler currently owns it, and ownership moves around as flights close, as a chute is taken for a late transfer, or as a bay is handed back. Each chute carries a small compare-and-swap version register, and the version advances every time ownership changes — both when a handler takes a chute and when a chute is handed back.

Handlers are slow but they do not fail. A handler always finishes what it started, but it may take a long time about it: it prepares a divert command against a chute, recording the chute's version at the moment it prepared, and only later gets around to committing that command to the belt controller. In between, the chute may well have been handed to somebody else. A handler prepares at most one command at a time.

The belt controller therefore re-checks at commit time. A prepared command is committed only if the chute's version register still holds the value the command recorded and the chute is still owned by the handler that prepared it. When it commits, the chute records the divert together with the handler that issued it and the version it was issued under. A command that fails either check is voided rather than committed, and the handler is free to prepare a fresh one.

The full set of actions is: Take, in which a handler takes ownership of an unowned chute, advancing that chute's version; Prepare, in which a handler that owns a chute and has nothing prepared records a divert command against it, capturing the chute's current version; Commit, in which a prepared command whose recorded version still matches and whose chute is still owned by its preparer is written to the chute as the standing divert; Void, in which a prepared command whose version is stale or whose chute has changed hands is thrown away; Hand, in which an owned chute is handed back, advancing its version; and Idle, in which the router simply waits once every chute's version register is used up and no handler has anything prepared.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every chute whose standing divert still carries the chute's current version is a chute that is still owned, and owned by exactly the handler that issued that divert, so no chute is left standing on a command from a handler that had already lost it.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: No handler is left with a prepared command forever — every command a handler prepares is eventually either committed or voided.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od7m6p1t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Cranes, Slots, NOLEASE

\* plan: the shared stow plan. record: the terminal's permanent list of
\* everything ever committed. lease: who may write. link: writes in flight,
\* taken up in whatever order the yard radio manages.
VARIABLES plan, record, lease, link

vars == <<plan, record, lease, link>>

Writes == [by: Cranes, saw: SUBSET Slots, add: Slots]

TypeOK ==
    /\ plan \subseteq Slots
    /\ record \subseteq Slots
    /\ lease \in Cranes \cup {NOLEASE}
    /\ link \subseteq Writes

Init ==
    /\ plan = {}
    /\ record = {}
    /\ lease = NOLEASE
    /\ link = {}

Outstanding(cr) == \E w \in link : w.by = cr

Grab(cr) ==
    /\ lease = NOLEASE
    /\ ~Outstanding(cr)
    /\ lease' = cr
    /\ UNCHANGED <<plan, record, link>>

\* Composing captures the copy this crane will later send back whole.
Compose(cr, s) ==
    /\ lease = cr
    /\ ~Outstanding(cr)
    /\ s \notin plan
    /\ link' = link \cup {[by |-> cr, saw |-> plan, add |-> s]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<plan, record, lease>>

\* The lease is checked when the write lands, not when it was composed.
Land(w) ==
    /\ w \in link
    /\ lease = w.by
    /\ plan' = w.saw \cup {w.add}
    /\ record' = record \cup {w.add}
    /\ link' = link \ {w}
    /\ lease' = NOLEASE

Bin(w) ==
    /\ w \in link
    /\ lease # w.by
    /\ link' = link \ {w}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<plan, record, lease>>

Expire ==
    /\ lease # NOLEASE
    /\ lease' = NOLEASE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<plan, record, link>>

Next ==
    \/ \E cr \in Cranes : Grab(cr)
    \/ \E cr \in Cranes, s \in Slots : Compose(cr, s)
    \/ \E w \in Writes : Land(w) \/ Bin(w)
    \/ Expire

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

CommittedSlotsSurvive == record \subseteq plan
====
nl:
A container terminal keeps one shared stow plan listing which bay slots on the berthed ship have been committed to cargo. Gantry cranes edit that plan, and because the plan is transmitted and stored as one document, an edit is a read-modify-write: a crane takes the plan as it stands, adds the slot it is about to fill, and sends the whole revised plan back to the planning office. That is the shape in which one crane's commitment can be wiped out by another crane's write.

Editing rights are handed out as a lease. Only the crane holding the lease may compose a write, and composing captures the copy of the plan the crane will send. Leases expire on their own, because a crane that stops working — driver change, a spreader fault, a wind stop — must not hold the plan shut.

Writes reach the planning office over the yard's radio link, which does not preserve order. Composed writes sit on the link and are taken up in whatever order they arrive, so a write composed under an earlier lease can arrive after a write composed under a later one. A crane has at most one write outstanding at a time.

The office therefore checks the lease when a write lands, not when it was composed. A write is applied only if its author is still the crane holding the lease; applying replaces the plan with exactly the copy that crane captured plus the slot it committed, notes the newly committed slot in the terminal's permanent commitment record, and gives the lease back. A write whose author no longer holds the lease is binned unapplied, because the copy it captured is no longer a safe basis for a whole-document overwrite.

The full set of actions is: Grab, in which a crane with no write outstanding takes the free editing lease; Compose, in which the lease-holding crane captures the current plan and picks a slot not yet in it, putting the resulting write onto the radio link; Land, in which a write whose author still holds the lease is applied, replacing the plan, recording the committed slot permanently, and releasing the lease; Bin, in which a write whose author no longer holds the lease is discarded unapplied; and Expire, in which an outstanding lease lapses on its own.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every slot in the terminal's permanent commitment record is still present in the shared stow plan, so no committed slot is ever erased by a crane writing back a copy of the plan taken before that commitment.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od0m8p6t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Teams, RoomCount, MinStaffed, NONE

Rooms == 1..RoomCount

\* listLock: the coarse day-list lock; roomLock: the fine per-room lock.
\* chit: what a team was told when it took the room lock.
\* booked: which team each room is scheduled to; staffed: rooms open now.
VARIABLES listLock, roomLock, chit, booked, staffed

vars == <<listLock, roomLock, chit, booked, staffed>>

Chits == [room: Rooms, sawStaffed: MinStaffed..RoomCount]

TypeOK ==
    /\ listLock \in Teams \cup {NONE}
    /\ roomLock \in [Rooms -> Teams \cup {NONE}]
    /\ chit \in [Teams -> Chits \cup {NONE}]
    /\ booked \in [Rooms -> Teams \cup {NONE}]
    /\ staffed \in MinStaffed..RoomCount

Init ==
    /\ listLock = NONE
    /\ roomLock = [r \in Rooms |-> NONE]
    /\ chit = [t \in Teams |-> NONE]
    /\ booked = [r \in Rooms |-> NONE]
    /\ staffed = MinStaffed

TakeList(t) ==
    /\ listLock = NONE
    /\ chit[t] = NONE
    /\ listLock' = t
    /\ UNCHANGED <<roomLock, chit, booked, staffed>>

\* The coarse lock is given up in the same step the chit is issued.
TakeRoom(t, r) ==
    /\ listLock = t
    /\ roomLock[r] = NONE
    /\ r <= staffed
    /\ booked[r] = NONE
    /\ roomLock' = [roomLock EXCEPT ![r] = t]
    /\ listLock' = NONE
    /\ chit' = [chit EXCEPT ![t] = [room |-> r, sawStaffed |-> staffed]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<booked, staffed>>

\* Book trusts the chit; what it verifies is that the chit is not stale.
Book(t) ==
    /\ chit[t] # NONE
    /\ chit[t].sawStaffed = staffed
    /\ roomLock[chit[t].room] = t
    /\ booked' = [booked EXCEPT ![chit[t].room] = t]
    /\ roomLock' = [roomLock EXCEPT ![chit[t].room] = NONE]
    /\ chit' = [chit EXCEPT ![t] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<listLock, staffed>>

Scrap(t) ==
    /\ chit[t] # NONE
    /\ chit[t].sawStaffed # staffed
    /\ roomLock' = [roomLock EXCEPT ![chit[t].room] = NONE]
    /\ chit' = [chit EXCEPT ![t] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<listLock, booked, staffed>>

Vacate(r) ==
    /\ booked[r] # NONE
    /\ booked' = [booked EXCEPT ![r] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<listLock, roomLock, chit, staffed>>

Restaff ==
    /\ \E n \in MinStaffed..RoomCount :
        /\ \A r \in Rooms : booked[r] # NONE => r <= n
        /\ staffed' = n
    /\ UNCHANGED <<listLock, roomLock, chit, booked>>

Next ==
    \/ \E t \in Teams : TakeList(t) \/ Book(t) \/ Scrap(t)
    \/ \E t \in Teams, r \in Rooms : TakeRoom(t, r)
    \/ \E r \in Rooms : Vacate(r)
    \/ Restaff

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
        /\ \A t \in Teams : SF_vars(Book(t)) /\ SF_vars(Scrap(t))

BookedRoomsAreStaffed ==
    \A r \in Rooms : booked[r] # NONE => r <= staffed

NoChitIsHeldForever ==
    \A t \in Teams : (chit[t] # NONE) ~> (chit[t] = NONE)
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Teams = {teamRed, teamBlue}
    RoomCount = 2
    MinStaffed = 1
    NONE = NONE

INVARIANT BookedRoomsAreStaffed

PROPERTY NoChitIsHeldForever
nl:
A hospital operating-room scheduler assigns surgical teams to rooms on the day list. Rooms are numbered, and how many of them are actually staffed is a live figure: the theatre coordinator opens and closes rooms through the day as anaesthetic and recovery staff arrive or are pulled away. Rooms above the staffed figure are shut, and nothing may be booked into them.

Booking goes through two levels of lock. A team must first take the day-list lock, which is the coarse one, and only while holding it may it take the lock on a single room. Taking the room lock releases the day-list lock at once, so the coarse lock is held only long enough to pick a room, and it also issues the team a chit recording the room it picked and the staffed figure as it stood at that moment.

The booking step trusts the chit rather than re-reading the board. That is deliberate: the whole reason the team was given a chit is so it does not have to go back to the coarse structure. What the booking step does check is that the staffed figure on the chit still equals the staffed figure now in force. If the coordinator has changed staffing since the chit was issued, the chit describes a board that no longer exists, so the team scraps it and gives the room lock back rather than booking against it. A team carries at most one chit.

The coordinator may restaff at any time, but never below a room that already carries a booking, because a team already scheduled into a room cannot be turned out by a staffing change.

The full set of actions is: TakeList, in which a team carrying no chit takes the free day-list lock; TakeRoom, in which a team holding the day-list lock takes a free room lock, releases the day-list lock, and receives a chit naming that room and the current staffed figure; Book, in which a team whose chit still matches the staffed figure books the room to itself, consuming the chit and releasing the room lock; Scrap, in which a team whose chit no longer matches the staffed figure discards it and releases the room lock unbooked; Vacate, in which a booked room's booking is cleared when the case finishes; and Restaff, in which the coordinator sets the staffed figure to any supported value that still covers every booked room.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every room that carries a booking is a room within the currently staffed figure, so no team is ever scheduled into a shut room on the strength of a chit the staffing has already overtaken.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: No team is left holding a chit forever — every chit issued is eventually either booked or scrapped.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od6m4p2t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Arrivals, MinDepth, MaxDepth

\* lobby / riding / delivered / stairs: the four tallies outside the queue.
\* queue: admitted groups, each a headcount, taken from the front.
\* depth: the queue's admission limit, retuned while the rush runs.
VARIABLES lobby, queue, riding, delivered, stairs, depth

vars == <<lobby, queue, riding, delivered, stairs, depth>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ lobby \in 0..Arrivals
    /\ queue \in Seq(1..Arrivals)
    /\ riding \in 0..Arrivals
    /\ delivered \in 0..Arrivals
    /\ stairs \in 0..Arrivals
    /\ depth \in MinDepth..MaxDepth

Init ==
    /\ lobby = Arrivals
    /\ queue = <<>>
    /\ riding = 0
    /\ delivered = 0
    /\ stairs = 0
    /\ depth = MinDepth

Queued ==
    LET add[i \in 0..Len(queue)] ==
        IF i = 0 THEN 0 ELSE queue[i] + add[i - 1]
    IN add[Len(queue)]

Admit(n) ==
    /\ Len(queue) < depth
    /\ n <= lobby
    /\ lobby' = lobby - n
    /\ queue' = Append(queue, n)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<riding, delivered, stairs, depth>>

\* Backpressure: nobody is admitted, and somebody in the lobby gives up.
Balk ==
    /\ Len(queue) >= depth
    /\ lobby > 0
    /\ lobby' = lobby - 1
    /\ stairs' = stairs + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, riding, delivered, depth>>

Board ==
    /\ queue # <<>>
    /\ riding' = riding + Head(queue)
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lobby, delivered, stairs, depth>>

Deliver(n) ==
    /\ n <= riding
    /\ riding' = riding - n
    /\ delivered' = delivered + n
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lobby, queue, stairs, depth>>

Retune ==
    /\ \E d \in MinDepth..MaxDepth : depth' = d
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lobby, queue, riding, delivered, stairs>>

Next ==
    \/ \E n \in 1..Arrivals : Admit(n) \/ Deliver(n)
    \/ Balk \/ Board \/ Retune

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

EveryoneIsAccountedFor ==
    lobby + Queued + riding + delivered + stairs = Arrivals
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Arrivals = 3
    MinDepth = 1
    MaxDepth = 2

INVARIANT EveryoneIsAccountedFor
nl:
An elevator bank in a skyscraper handles the morning rush through a dispatch queue. Every person who walks into the lobby during the rush is accounted for by the building's people-counting system, and the count is what the facilities team audits at the end of the peak: nobody may be double-counted and nobody may vanish. At any instant a person is in exactly one of five places — still standing in the lobby, folded into a group that has been admitted to the dispatch queue, riding in a car, delivered to their floor, or gone, having given up and walked to the stairs.

The dispatch queue is bounded and admits groups rather than individuals: the dispatcher takes some of the people standing in the lobby and admits them as one group at the back of the queue. The queue's depth limit is retuned live, because the bank runs a shallower queue when a car is out of service and a deeper one when all cars are running.

Backpressure is what happens when the queue is at its depth limit: the dispatcher stops admitting, and a person left standing in a lobby that is going nowhere gives up and takes the stairs. That person is not lost from the count — they move to the gone tally, which is exactly what makes the end-of-peak audit balance.

Groups leave the queue from the front. The bank takes the front group into the cars all at once, and people riding in the cars are delivered to their floors as the cars stop.

The full set of actions is: Admit, in which the dispatcher takes some of the people standing in the lobby and puts them into the queue as one group, permitted only while the queue is below its current depth limit; Balk, in which a person still standing in the lobby gives up and walks to the stairs, permitted only while the queue is at its depth limit; Board, in which the front group of the queue is taken into the cars; Deliver, in which some of the people riding reach their floors; and Retune, in which the bank sets the queue's depth limit to any supported value.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The people still standing in the lobby, plus the people in all the groups sitting in the dispatch queue, plus the people riding in the cars, plus the people delivered to their floors, plus the people who gave up and took the stairs, always add up to exactly the number the people-counting system recorded entering.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od3m0p5t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Instructions, LogLimit, NONE

\* version: the ledger value the optimistic check compares against.
\* log: the settlement log; landedAt: where each instruction settled.
\* network: commit requests in flight, arriving in no particular order.
VARIABLES version, log, landedAt, network

vars == <<version, log, landedAt, network>>

Requests == [ins: Instructions, base: 0..LogLimit]

TypeOK ==
    /\ version \in 0..LogLimit
    /\ log \in Seq(Instructions)
    /\ landedAt \in [Instructions -> (1..LogLimit) \cup {NONE}]
    /\ network \subseteq Requests

Init ==
    /\ version = 0
    /\ log = <<>>
    /\ landedAt = [i \in Instructions |-> NONE]
    /\ network = {}

Pending(i) == \E r \in network : r.ins = i

Prepare(i) ==
    /\ landedAt[i] = NONE
    /\ ~Pending(i)
    /\ network' = network \cup {[ins |-> i, base |-> version]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, log, landedAt>>

\* The optimistic check: the version read must still be the version now.
Settle(r) ==
    /\ r \in network
    /\ r.base = version
    /\ landedAt[r.ins] = NONE
    /\ Len(log) < LogLimit
    /\ log' = Append(log, r.ins)
    /\ landedAt' = [landedAt EXCEPT ![r.ins] = Len(log) + 1]
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ network' = network \ {r}

Retry(r) ==
    /\ r \in network
    /\ landedAt[r.ins] = NONE
    /\ \/ r.base # version
       \/ Len(log) >= LogLimit
    /\ network' = network \ {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, log, landedAt>>

Drop(r) ==
    /\ r \in network
    /\ landedAt[r.ins] # NONE
    /\ network' = network \ {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, log, landedAt>>

\* Everything has settled and nothing is in flight: the cycle is closed.
Closed ==
    /\ network = {}
    /\ \A i \in Instructions : landedAt[i] # NONE
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E i \in Instructions : Prepare(i)
    \/ \E r \in Requests : Settle(r) \/ Retry(r) \/ Drop(r)
    \/ Closed

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
        /\ \A r \in Requests :
            WF_vars(Settle(r)) /\ WF_vars(Retry(r)) /\ WF_vars(Drop(r))

LogPositionsMatchRecords ==
    \A i \in 1..Len(log) : landedAt[log[i]] = i

NoRequestSitsOnTheNetwork ==
    \A r \in Requests : (r \in network) ~> (r \notin network)
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Instructions = {mt103a, mt103b}
    LogLimit = 2
    NONE = NONE

INVARIANT LogPositionsMatchRecords

PROPERTY NoRequestSitsOnTheNetwork
nl:
A clearing bank settles interbank payment instructions against a central ledger. Settling an instruction is irreversible: the funds move across the central bank's books and there is no unwind, so an instruction that settles twice is a duplicated payment that has to be chased manually between two institutions.

The ledger is not locked while an instruction is being prepared. The bank works optimistically instead: a member reads the ledger's current version, prepares a commit request naming the instruction and the version it read, and sends it in. Requests reach the ledger over the settlement network, which does not preserve order — a request prepared earlier can arrive after one prepared later. A member has at most one request outstanding for a given instruction.

The ledger accepts a request only if the version it names is still the ledger's version and the instruction has not already settled. Accepting appends the instruction to the settlement log, advances the version by one, and records against that instruction the position in the log where it landed. A request naming a superseded version is not settled; it is simply dropped, and the member is free to read the ledger again and prepare a fresh one — that is what optimistic working means here. A request for an instruction that has already settled is dropped as well, because the payment has already moved. The settlement log runs to a fixed length for the cycle, and once it is full no further requests can be accepted, so those are dropped for retry in the next cycle too.

The full set of actions is: Prepare, in which a member reads the ledger's version and puts a commit request for an unsettled instruction onto the settlement network; Settle, in which the ledger accepts a request whose version still matches, appending its instruction to the log, advancing the version, and recording the log position against that instruction; Retry, in which a request naming a superseded version, or arriving when the log is already full, is dropped so it can be prepared again; Drop, in which a request for an instruction that has already settled is discarded; and Closed, in which the ledger simply waits once every instruction has settled and nothing is left in flight.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every position in the settlement log, the instruction sitting there has that exact position recorded against it as the place it settled, so no instruction appears in the log more than once and no payment settles twice.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: No commit request sits on the settlement network forever — every request that is sent in is eventually taken off it, whether by settling, by being dropped for retry, or by being discarded as already settled.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od5m9p0t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Regions, Servers, MaxEpoch, NONE

\* fleetEpoch: the reconfiguration epoch of the server fleet.
\* grant: which region each server is granted to; stamp: the epoch that
\* grant was written under. hosting: the server each region is running on.
VARIABLES fleetEpoch, grant, stamp, hosting

vars == <<fleetEpoch, grant, stamp, hosting>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ fleetEpoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ grant \in [Servers -> Regions \cup {NONE}]
    /\ stamp \in [Servers -> 0..MaxEpoch]
    /\ hosting \in [Regions -> Servers \cup {NONE}]

Init ==
    /\ fleetEpoch = 0
    /\ grant = [s \in Servers |-> NONE]
    /\ stamp = [s \in Servers |-> 0]
    /\ hosting = [r \in Regions |-> NONE]

Grant(r, s) ==
    /\ grant[s] = NONE
    /\ hosting[r] = NONE
    /\ grant' = [grant EXCEPT ![s] = r]
    /\ stamp' = [stamp EXCEPT ![s] = fleetEpoch]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fleetEpoch, hosting>>

\* A match starts only on this region's own grant, at the current epoch.
Occupy(r, s) ==
    /\ hosting[r] = NONE
    /\ grant[s] = r
    /\ stamp[s] = fleetEpoch
    /\ hosting' = [hosting EXCEPT ![r] = s]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fleetEpoch, grant, stamp>>

Finish(r) ==
    /\ hosting[r] # NONE
    /\ grant' = [grant EXCEPT ![hosting[r]] = NONE]
    /\ hosting' = [hosting EXCEPT ![r] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fleetEpoch, stamp>>

Revoke(s) ==
    /\ grant[s] # NONE
    /\ stamp[s] # fleetEpoch
    /\ \A r \in Regions : hosting[r] # s
    /\ grant' = [grant EXCEPT ![s] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fleetEpoch, stamp, hosting>>

\* Draining is a precondition of the epoch bump, never a consequence of it.
Reconfigure ==
    /\ fleetEpoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ \A r \in Regions : hosting[r] = NONE
    /\ fleetEpoch' = fleetEpoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<grant, stamp, hosting>>

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Regions, s \in Servers : Grant(r, s) \/ Occupy(r, s)
    \/ \E r \in Regions : Finish(r)
    \/ \E s \in Servers : Revoke(s)
    \/ Reconfigure

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

RunningMatchHoldsItsGrant ==
    \A r \in Regions : hosting[r] # NONE => grant[hosting[r]] = r
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Regions = {euWest, naEast}
    Servers = {srvOne, srvTwo}
    MaxEpoch = 2
    NONE = NONE

INVARIANT RunningMatchHoldsItsGrant
nl:
A game publisher runs two matchmaking regions that make their own decisions independently — the European region and the North American one — but both draw dedicated game servers from a single shared server pool. A dedicated server is the critical resource here: it hosts one match at a time, and two regions starting matches on the same box is a live incident, not a scheduling inefficiency.

The pool hands out grants. A region asks the pool for a server, the pool records that server as granted to that region, and only then may the region put a match on it. A region runs at most one match at a time, and asks for a server only while it is not running one. Finishing a match takes the region off the server and gives the grant back.

The server fleet is reconfigured under an epoch number: boxes are drained for patching, a new rack comes online, the capacity plan changes. Every reconfiguration advances the fleet epoch, and each grant carries the epoch it was issued under, so a grant written against the old fleet layout is recognisably stale. A stale grant is revoked rather than honoured, and a region can only put a match on a server whose grant is both its own and current.

The one thing the publisher will not do is reconfigure the fleet underneath a running match. A reconfiguration is only permitted while no region is running a match at all — draining is a precondition of the epoch bump, not a consequence of it — because advancing the epoch invalidates grants, and invalidating the grant under a live match is exactly how the same box ends up handed to the other region.

The full set of actions is: Grant, in which the pool grants an ungranted server to a region that is not running a match, stamping the grant with the current fleet epoch; Occupy, in which a region with no match running starts one on a server whose grant is its own and carries the current epoch; Finish, in which a region's match ends, taking it off the server and returning the grant to the pool; Revoke, in which a grant stamped with a superseded epoch is taken back; and Reconfigure, in which the fleet advances to the next epoch, permitted only while no region is running a match.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever a region is running a match on a server, the pool's books show that server granted to exactly that region, so the two regions can never both be running matches on the same box.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od13m1p5t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS MachineCount, MaxGen, NOBODY, NODECISION

Machines == 1..MachineCount

\* token: the ring position of the payout token.
\* pending: each machine's outstanding decision, carrying the claim
\* generation it saw. gen: the register's claim generation.
\* winner: the register's record. paidOut: each machine's own note.
VARIABLES token, pending, gen, winner, paidOut

vars == <<token, pending, gen, winner, paidOut>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ token \in Machines
    /\ pending \in [Machines -> (0..MaxGen) \cup {NODECISION}]
    /\ gen \in 0..MaxGen
    /\ winner \in Machines \cup {NOBODY}
    /\ paidOut \in [Machines -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
    /\ token = 1
    /\ pending = [m \in Machines |-> NODECISION]
    /\ gen = 0
    /\ winner = NOBODY
    /\ paidOut = [m \in Machines |-> FALSE]

Decide(m) ==
    /\ token = m
    /\ pending[m] = NODECISION
    /\ winner = NOBODY
    /\ pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![m] = gen]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, gen, winner, paidOut>>

\* The payout trusts the decision only while its generation still stands.
Pay(m) ==
    /\ pending[m] # NODECISION
    /\ pending[m] = gen
    /\ token = m
    /\ gen < MaxGen
    /\ winner' = m
    /\ paidOut' = [paidOut EXCEPT ![m] = TRUE]
    /\ gen' = gen + 1
    /\ pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![m] = NODECISION]
    /\ UNCHANGED token

Drop(m) ==
    /\ pending[m] # NODECISION
    /\ \/ pending[m] # gen
       \/ token # m
    /\ pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![m] = NODECISION]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, gen, winner, paidOut>>

Pass ==
    /\ token' = (token % MachineCount) + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pending, gen, winner, paidOut>>

Next ==
    \/ Pass
    \/ \E m \in Machines : Decide(m) \/ Pay(m) \/ Drop(m)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
        /\ WF_vars(Pass)
        /\ \A m \in Machines : SF_vars(Pay(m)) /\ WF_vars(Drop(m))

OnlyTheRegisteredWinnerPaid ==
    \A m \in Machines : paidOut[m] => winner = m

NoDecisionIsLeftOutstanding ==
    \A m \in Machines : (pending[m] # NODECISION) ~> (pending[m] = NODECISION)
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    MachineCount = 3
    MaxGen = 2
    NOBODY = NOBODY
    NODECISION = NODECISION

INVARIANT OnlyTheRegisteredWinnerPaid

PROPERTY NoDecisionIsLeftOutstanding
nl:
A vending machine network runs a promotion with a single grand prize. Paying the grand prize out is irreversible — the machine opens the prize bay, the customer walks off with it, and there is no recalling it — and the promotion is funded for exactly one payout across the whole estate. Two machines paying it out is a loss the operator eats.

The machines take turns at the prize register using a token ring: they are wired in a ring, one payout token circulates, and a machine may only touch the register while it holds the token. The token keeps moving around the ring whether or not anybody is doing anything with it.

Machines are slow but they do not fail. A machine decides to pay out the prize while it holds the token and while the register still shows the prize unclaimed, but the actual payout comes later, after the coin mechanism has cycled and the bay has unlatched. In the meantime the token may have gone right around the ring and another machine may have paid the prize out already.

That is why the register carries a claim generation, which advances every time the prize is paid. A machine's decision records the generation it saw. When the machine is finally ready, it pays out only if the generation on its decision still matches the register and it still holds the token; the register then records that machine as the winner and advances the generation, and the machine notes internally that it was the one that paid. A decision whose generation has moved on, or whose machine no longer holds the token, is dropped rather than acted on.

The full set of actions is: Decide, in which the machine holding the token, with no decision outstanding, sees the prize unclaimed and records a decision carrying the register's current claim generation; Pay, in which a machine whose decision still carries the register's generation and which still holds the token pays the prize out, is recorded as the winner, advances the generation, and notes internally that it paid; Drop, in which a decision whose generation has moved on, or whose machine no longer holds the token, is discarded; and Pass, in which the payout token moves on to the next machine around the ring.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any machine whose own records say it paid the prize out is the machine the register names as the winner, so the grand prize is never paid out by two machines.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: No machine is left with an outstanding decision forever — every decision a machine records is eventually either paid out or dropped.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od14m8p2t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Drones, Bays, Inventory, NONE

\* store: cells racked in the depot; cradle: cells staged per bay;
\* onboard: cells fitted per drone. depotLock is coarse, bayLock is fine.
VARIABLES store, cradle, onboard, depotLock, bayLock

vars == <<store, cradle, onboard, depotLock, bayLock>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ store \in 0..Inventory
    /\ cradle \in [Bays -> 0..Inventory]
    /\ onboard \in [Drones -> 0..Inventory]
    /\ depotLock \in Drones \cup {NONE}
    /\ bayLock \in [Bays -> Drones \cup {NONE}]

Init ==
    /\ store = Inventory
    /\ cradle = [b \in Bays |-> 0]
    /\ onboard = [d \in Drones |-> 0]
    /\ depotLock = NONE
    /\ bayLock = [b \in Bays |-> NONE]

SumOver(f, S) ==
    LET add[T \in SUBSET S] ==
        IF T = {} THEN 0
        ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in T : TRUE IN f[x] + add[T \ {x}]
    IN add[S]

TakeDepot(d) ==
    /\ depotLock = NONE
    /\ depotLock' = d
    /\ UNCHANGED <<store, cradle, onboard, bayLock>>

\* The coarse lock is released in the same step the bay lock is taken.
TakeBay(d, b) ==
    /\ depotLock = d
    /\ bayLock[b] = NONE
    /\ bayLock' = [bayLock EXCEPT ![b] = d]
    /\ depotLock' = NONE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<store, cradle, onboard>>

DropDepot(d) ==
    /\ depotLock = d
    /\ depotLock' = NONE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<store, cradle, onboard, bayLock>>

Stage(d, b, n) ==
    /\ bayLock[b] = d
    /\ n <= store
    /\ store' = store - n
    /\ cradle' = [cradle EXCEPT ![b] = @ + n]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<onboard, depotLock, bayLock>>

Fit(d, b, n) ==
    /\ bayLock[b] = d
    /\ n <= cradle[b]
    /\ cradle' = [cradle EXCEPT ![b] = @ - n]
    /\ onboard' = [onboard EXCEPT ![d] = @ + n]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<store, depotLock, bayLock>>

Hand(d, b, n) ==
    /\ bayLock[b] = d
    /\ n <= onboard[d]
    /\ onboard' = [onboard EXCEPT ![d] = @ - n]
    /\ store' = store + n
    /\ UNCHANGED <<cradle, depotLock, bayLock>>

\* Nothing takes a bay lock away from a slow drone; it gives it back itself.
ReleaseBay(d, b) ==
    /\ bayLock[b] = d
    /\ bayLock' = [bayLock EXCEPT ![b] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<store, cradle, onboard, depotLock>>

Next ==
    \/ \E d \in Drones : TakeDepot(d) \/ DropDepot(d)
    \/ \E d \in Drones, b \in Bays : TakeBay(d, b) \/ ReleaseBay(d, b)
    \/ \E d \in Drones, b \in Bays, n \in 1..Inventory :
        Stage(d, b, n) \/ Fit(d, b, n) \/ Hand(d, b, n)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

CellsAreConserved ==
    store + SumOver(cradle, Bays) + SumOver(onboard, Drones) = Inventory
====

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Drones = {scoutA, scoutB}
    Bays = {bay1, bay2}
    Inventory = 2
    NONE = NONE

INVARIANT CellsAreConserved
nl:
A wildfire surveillance swarm operates from a forward base with a fixed inventory of fuel cells. A fuel cell is a physical brick: at any instant every cell the base holds is either racked in the depot store, staged in one of the servicing bays' cradles, or fitted in a drone. The base commander's inventory board has to balance at the end of every sortie, so cells are never conjured and never written off mid-operation.

Access to the depot is arranged with a two-level lock, because a drone that walks in and helps itself while another is mid-transfer is how cells go missing off the board. A drone must first take the depot lock, which is the coarse one covering the whole store, and only while holding it may it take the lock on one servicing bay. Taking a bay's lock releases the depot lock immediately, so no drone sits on the whole store while it works one bay.

Holding a bay's lock is what lets a drone move cells: it may draw cells from the depot store into that bay's cradle, fit cells from the cradle into itself, and hand cells it is carrying back to the depot store. Every one of those movements takes cells out of one place and puts the same number into another.

Drones are slow but they do not fail. A drone that has taken a bay's lock will eventually give it back, but it may be a long while — a thermal scan is running, the airframe is cooling, telemetry is backed up — and nothing takes the lock away from it in the meantime. A drone that has taken the depot lock but decided against a bay simply drops it.

The full set of actions is: TakeDepot, in which a drone takes the free depot lock; TakeBay, in which a drone holding the depot lock takes a free bay lock and releases the depot lock in the same step; DropDepot, in which a drone releases the depot lock without taking a bay; Stage, in which a drone holding a bay's lock draws cells from the depot store into that bay's cradle; Fit, in which a drone holding a bay's lock fits cells from that cradle into itself; Hand, in which a drone holding a bay's lock returns cells it is carrying to the depot store; and ReleaseBay, in which a drone gives a bay's lock back.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The fuel cells racked in the depot store, plus those staged in the bay cradles, plus those fitted in the drones, always add up to exactly the inventory the forward base holds.

---- MODULE W4Od18m0p2t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Locks, TotalCharge, MaxVersion, MaxRetry

\* charge: units held at each lock. mesh: donations in flight, taken up in
\* no particular order. version: the optimistic stamp each lock exposes.
\* retries: how many failed attempts a donor has already absorbed.
VARIABLES charge, version, mesh, retries

vars == <<charge, version, mesh, retries>>

Donations == [from: Locks, to: Locks, amt: 1..TotalCharge,
              seen: 0..MaxVersion]

TypeOK ==
    /\ charge \in [Locks -> 0..TotalCharge]
    /\ version \in [Locks -> 0..MaxVersion]
    /\ mesh \subseteq Donations
    /\ retries \in [Locks -> 0..MaxRetry]

Start == CHOOSE l \in Locks : TRUE

Init ==
    /\ charge = [l \in Locks |-> IF l = Start THEN TotalCharge ELSE 0]
    /\ version = [l \in Locks |-> 0]
    /\ mesh = {}
    /\ retries = [l \in Locks |-> 0]

Held ==
    LET add[S \in SUBSET Locks] ==
        IF S = {} THEN 0
        ELSE LET l == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE IN charge[l] + add[S \ {l}]
    IN add[Locks]

RECURSIVE SumAmt(_)
SumAmt(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET d == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE IN d.amt + SumAmt(S \ {d})

Flying == SumAmt(mesh)

\* The donor debits itself the moment the units go onto the mesh.
Donate(a, b, n) ==
    /\ a # b
    /\ n <= charge[a]
    /\ retries[a] < MaxRetry
    /\ ~(\E d \in mesh : d.from = a /\ d.to = b)
    /\ charge' = [charge EXCEPT ![a] = @ - n]
    /\ mesh' = mesh \cup {[from |-> a, to |-> b, amt |-> n,
                           seen |-> version[b]]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, retries>>

Credit(d) ==
    /\ d \in mesh
    /\ version[d.to] = d.seen
    /\ charge' = [charge EXCEPT ![d.to] = @ + d.amt]
    /\ mesh' = mesh \ {d}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, retries>>

\* A stale donation goes back whole; units are never split or shaved.
Return(d) ==
    /\ d \in mesh
    /\ version[d.to] # d.seen
    /\ charge' = [charge EXCEPT ![d.from] = @ + d.amt]
    /\ mesh' = mesh \ {d}
    /\ retries' = [retries EXCEPT ![d.from] =
                       IF @ < MaxRetry THEN @ + 1 ELSE @]
    /\ UNCHANGED version

Bump(l) ==
    /\ version[l] < MaxVersion
    /\ version' = [version EXCEPT ![l] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<charge, mesh, retries>>

\* Nothing in flight and no stamp left to move: the mesh is quiet.
Quiet ==
    /\ mesh = {}
    /\ \A l \in Locks : version[l] = MaxVersion
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E a, b \in Locks : \E n \in 1..TotalCharge : Donate(a, b, n)
    \/ \E d \in Donations : Credit(d) \/ Return(d)
    \/ \E l \in Locks : Bump(l)
    \/ Quiet

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
        /\ \A d \in Donations : WF_vars(Credit(d)) /\ WF_vars(Return(d))

ChargeIsConserved == Held + Flying = TotalCharge

NoDonationStaysOnTheMesh ==
    \A d \in Donations : (d \in mesh) ~> (d \notin mesh)
====

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Locks = {frontLock, patioLock}
    TotalCharge = 2
    MaxVersion = 1
    MaxRetry = 2

INVARIANT ChargeIsConserved

PROPERTY NoDonationStaysOnTheMesh
nl:
A smart-home door lock network shares battery charge between its locks peer to peer, with no hub holding a reserve. Charge is measured in whole units and the installed total is fixed for the day: every unit is either sitting in one of the locks or riding in a donation that one lock has sent to another and that has not yet been taken up.

Donations travel over the home's mesh radio, which does not preserve order. Several donations can be in the air at once and they are taken up in whatever order the mesh manages, so a donation sent first may well arrive last. A lock will not have more than one donation outstanding to the same neighbour at a time. The donor debits itself the moment it sends — the units are physically committed to the transfer — and each donation records the version number the receiving lock was showing when the donation was composed.

There is no lock held over the receiver while a donation is in flight. The network works optimistically instead: when a donation is taken up, the receiver compares the version it recorded against its own version now. If they match, the units are credited to the receiver. If they do not — the receiver has re-paired, had its keypad re-keyed, or taken a firmware bump in the meantime — the donation is not credited; the units go back whole to the donor, who is free to compose a fresh donation against the receiver's new version. That is what retrying means here: nothing is held, nothing is lost, the transfer is simply attempted again.

Retrying is not free. Each returned donation counts against the donor's retry budget, and a lock that has used its budget up stops composing new donations for the rest of the day rather than churning the mesh.

The full set of actions is: Donate, in which a lock with retry budget left debits itself and puts a donation to a neighbour onto the mesh, recording that neighbour's current version, provided it has none outstanding to that neighbour; Credit, in which a receiving lock takes up a donation whose recorded version still matches and adds the units to its own charge; Return, in which a donation whose recorded version no longer matches its receiver is taken off the mesh, its units given back whole to the donor, and the donor's retry budget charged; Bump, in which a lock's version advances because it was re-paired or re-keyed; and Quiet, in which the network simply rests once nothing is in flight and no lock has any version change left to make.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The charge units held across all the locks, plus the units riding in donations still on the mesh, always add up to exactly the total the installer configured.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: No donation stays on the mesh forever — every donation that is sent is eventually taken off it, either credited to its receiver or returned to its donor.

---- MODULE W4Od15m6p4t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Members, Symbols, SessionLimit, MaxEpoch

\* open: sessions running against each symbol's book.
\* link: grants in flight, taken up in no particular order.
\* era: each symbol's admission epoch, advanced when a lease lapses.
\* halted: symbols suspended for a volatility interruption.
VARIABLES open, link, era, halted

vars == <<open, link, era, halted>>

Grants == [member: Members, symbol: Symbols, era: 0..MaxEpoch]

TypeOK ==
    /\ open \in [Symbols -> SUBSET Members]
    /\ link \subseteq Grants
    /\ era \in [Symbols -> 0..MaxEpoch]
    /\ halted \subseteq Symbols

Init ==
    /\ open = [s \in Symbols |-> {}]
    /\ link = {}
    /\ era = [s \in Symbols |-> 0]
    /\ halted = {}

\* A grant counts against the limit from the instant it is issued.
Outstanding(s) == {g \in link : g.symbol = s /\ g.era = era[s]}
Committed(s) == Cardinality(open[s]) + Cardinality(Outstanding(s))

Issue(m, s) ==
    /\ s \notin halted
    /\ m \notin open[s]
    /\ ~(\E g \in link : g.member = m /\ g.symbol = s)
    /\ Committed(s) < SessionLimit
    /\ link' = link \cup {[member |-> m, symbol |-> s, era |-> era[s]]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<open, era, halted>>

TakeUp(g) ==
    /\ g \in link
    /\ g.symbol \notin halted
    /\ g.era = era[g.symbol]
    /\ open' = [open EXCEPT ![g.symbol] = @ \cup {g.member}]
    /\ link' = link \ {g}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<era, halted>>

Discard(g) ==
    /\ g \in link
    /\ g.era # era[g.symbol]
    /\ link' = link \ {g}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<open, era, halted>>

\* Lapsing advances the epoch, which retires every grant written against it.
Lapse(m, s) ==
    /\ m \in open[s]
    /\ era[s] < MaxEpoch
    /\ open' = [open EXCEPT ![s] = @ \ {m}]
    /\ era' = [era EXCEPT ![s] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<link, halted>>

Surrender(m, s) ==
    /\ m \in open[s]
    /\ open' = [open EXCEPT ![s] = @ \ {m}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<link, era, halted>>

Halt(s) ==
    /\ s \notin halted
    /\ halted' = halted \cup {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<open, link, era>>

Resume(s) ==
    /\ s \in halted
    /\ halted' = halted \ {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<open, link, era>>

Next ==
    \/ \E m \in Members, s \in Symbols :
        Issue(m, s) \/ Lapse(m, s) \/ Surrender(m, s)
    \/ \E g \in Grants : TakeUp(g) \/ Discard(g)
    \/ \E s \in Symbols : Halt(s) \/ Resume(s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

WithinSessionLimit == \A s \in Symbols : Committed(s) <= SessionLimit

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Members = {firmA, firmB}
    Symbols = {sym1, sym2}
    SessionLimit = 1
    MaxEpoch = 2

INVARIANT WithinSessionLimit
nl:
A stock exchange runs its opening auction with a hard limit on how many member firms may have an order-entry session open against any one symbol's book at the same time. The limit is a matching-engine capacity figure, not a policy preference: exceeding it means the book cannot be crossed within the auction window.

Sessions are handed out as leases. A member does not get a session by asking for one directly; the exchange puts a grant onto the member link, and the member's session begins when the grant is taken up. The member link does not preserve order, so grants are taken up in whatever order they arrive, and a grant issued earlier may be acted on later. A member has at most one grant outstanding per symbol.

Because a grant that has been issued but not yet taken up is a session that is going to exist, the exchange counts it against the symbol's capacity from the moment it issues it, not from the moment the member takes it up. Issuing a grant is only permitted while the sessions already open, counted together with the grants still outstanding for that symbol, leave room under the limit.

Each symbol carries an admission epoch, and a grant records the epoch in force when it was issued. Leases expire: a session that is not kept up lapses, and lapsing advances the symbol's epoch. That advance is what makes the accounting safe — every grant still outstanding for that symbol was written against the old epoch, so it can no longer be taken up and stops counting against the limit. A grant whose epoch no longer matches is simply taken off the link. A member may also give a session up voluntarily, which does not disturb the epoch.

Books can be halted for a volatility interruption. While a symbol is halted the exchange issues no new grants for it and takes up none of the outstanding ones; sessions already open are unaffected, and the halt is lifted when the interruption ends.

The full set of actions is: Issue, in which the exchange puts a grant for a member onto the link for an unhalted symbol, stamped with that symbol's epoch, provided the open sessions plus outstanding grants leave room under the limit; TakeUp, in which a grant whose epoch still matches its unhalted symbol is taken off the link and becomes an open session; Discard, in which a grant whose epoch no longer matches is taken off the link; Lapse, in which an open session expires, closing it and advancing that symbol's epoch; Surrender, in which a member closes an open session voluntarily; Halt, in which a symbol's book is suspended for a volatility interruption; and Resume, in which a halted symbol's book reopens.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every symbol, the sessions currently open against its book, counted together with the grants still outstanding at that symbol's current epoch, never exceed the matching engine's session limit.

---- MODULE W4Od15m8p0t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Firms, NOBODY

\* sessionLock: the coarse lock over the opening process.
\* engineLock: the fine lock on the matching engine itself.
\* uncrossing: each firm's own flag saying it is inside the engine.
\* asking: the queue of firms wanting the engine; logged: firms that finished.
VARIABLES sessionLock, engineLock, uncrossing, asking, logged

vars == <<sessionLock, engineLock, uncrossing, asking, logged>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ sessionLock \in Firms \cup {NOBODY}
    /\ engineLock \in Firms \cup {NOBODY}
    /\ uncrossing \in [Firms -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ asking \subseteq Firms
    /\ logged \subseteq Firms

Init ==
    /\ sessionLock = NOBODY
    /\ engineLock = NOBODY
    /\ uncrossing = [f \in Firms |-> FALSE]
    /\ asking = {}
    /\ logged = {}

Queue(f) ==
    /\ f \notin asking
    /\ ~uncrossing[f]
    /\ engineLock # f
    /\ sessionLock # f
    /\ asking' = asking \cup {f}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<sessionLock, engineLock, uncrossing, logged>>

TakeSession(f) ==
    /\ f \in asking
    /\ sessionLock = NOBODY
    /\ sessionLock' = f
    /\ asking' = asking \ {f}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<engineLock, uncrossing, logged>>

\* Reaching the engine gives up the coarse lock in the same step.
TakeEngine(f) ==
    /\ sessionLock = f
    /\ engineLock = NOBODY
    /\ engineLock' = f
    /\ sessionLock' = NOBODY
    /\ UNCHANGED <<uncrossing, asking, logged>>

DropSession(f) ==
    /\ sessionLock = f
    /\ sessionLock' = NOBODY
    /\ UNCHANGED <<engineLock, uncrossing, asking, logged>>

Start(f) ==
    /\ engineLock = f
    /\ ~uncrossing[f]
    /\ uncrossing' = [uncrossing EXCEPT ![f] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<sessionLock, engineLock, asking, logged>>

\* Nothing preempts a slow firm; it finishes and releases the engine itself.
Finish(f) ==
    /\ engineLock = f
    /\ uncrossing[f]
    /\ uncrossing' = [uncrossing EXCEPT ![f] = FALSE]
    /\ engineLock' = NOBODY
    /\ logged' = logged \cup {f}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<sessionLock, asking>>

Next ==
    \E f \in Firms :
        Queue(f) \/ TakeSession(f) \/ TakeEngine(f)
        \/ DropSession(f) \/ Start(f) \/ Finish(f)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
        /\ \A f \in Firms : WF_vars(Start(f)) /\ WF_vars(Finish(f))

UncrossingFirmHoldsTheEngine ==
    \A f \in Firms : uncrossing[f] => engineLock = f

EngineIsNeverHeldForever ==
    (engineLock # NOBODY) ~> (engineLock = NOBODY)

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Firms = {alphaCap, bravoSec}
    NOBODY = NOBODY

INVARIANT UncrossingFirmHoldsTheEngine

PROPERTY EngineIsNeverHeldForever
nl:
A stock exchange's opening auction ends with an uncrossing run on the matching engine. The engine is the critical resource: it walks the whole book computing the opening price, and two firms running uncrossings at the same time would produce two different opening prints.

Access is arranged in two levels. A firm that wants the engine first joins the queue of firms asking for it. From the queue it takes the auction session lock, which is the coarse one covering the whole opening process, and only while holding that may it take the engine lock itself. Taking the engine lock releases the session lock in the same step, so the coarse lock is held only long enough to reach the engine, and other firms can carry on queueing behind it.

Holding the engine lock is what lets a firm start uncrossing. A firm that has started keeps its own internal flag saying it is uncrossing, and clears that flag when it finishes; finishing also releases the engine lock and records that the firm has completed an uncrossing at least once in the day's log.

Firms are slow but they do not fail. A firm that has the engine lock may take a long time to get started and a long time to finish — its risk checks are slow, its book is large, its network is congested — but it always gets there in the end, and nothing takes the engine lock away from it in the meantime. A firm holding only the coarse session lock may also simply drop it without reaching the engine.

The full set of actions is: Queue, in which a firm that is not uncrossing joins the queue of firms asking for the engine; TakeSession, in which a queued firm takes the free session lock and leaves the queue; TakeEngine, in which a firm holding the session lock takes the free engine lock and releases the session lock in the same step; DropSession, in which a firm gives up the session lock without reaching the engine; Start, in which a firm holding the engine lock begins its uncrossing and raises its own flag; and Finish, in which a firm that is uncrossing lowers its flag, releases the engine lock, and is recorded in the day's log.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any firm whose own flag says it is uncrossing is the firm that currently holds the engine lock, so two firms are never uncrossing the book at the same time.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: The engine lock is never held forever — whenever a firm has taken it, it is eventually released again, because a slow firm still starts and still finishes.

---- MODULE W4Od3m7p4t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Engines, Ceiling, MaxVersion, NOREAD

\* drawn: liquidity actually taken; held: reserved but not yet drawn.
\* version: the shared register's compare-and-swap value.
\* view: what an engine read — the version and the headroom it saw.
VARIABLES drawn, held, version, view

vars == <<drawn, held, version, view>>

Views == [version: 0..MaxVersion, room: 0..Ceiling]

TypeOK ==
    /\ drawn \in [Engines -> 0..Ceiling]
    /\ held \in [Engines -> 0..Ceiling]
    /\ version \in 0..MaxVersion
    /\ view \in [Engines -> Views \cup {NOREAD}]

Init ==
    /\ drawn = [e \in Engines |-> 0]
    /\ held = [e \in Engines |-> 0]
    /\ version = 0
    /\ view = [e \in Engines |-> NOREAD]

Total(f) ==
    LET add[S \in SUBSET Engines] ==
        IF S = {} THEN 0
        ELSE LET e == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE IN f[e] + add[S \ {e}]
    IN add[Engines]

Exposure == Total(drawn) + Total(held)

Read(e) ==
    /\ view[e] = NOREAD
    /\ view' = [view EXCEPT ![e] =
                    [version |-> version, room |-> Ceiling - Exposure]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<drawn, held, version>>

\* The commit works from the headroom that was read, so the version check
\* is what stands between a stale view and an over-drawn pool.
Reserve(e, n) ==
    /\ view[e] # NOREAD
    /\ held[e] = 0
    /\ view[e].version = version
    /\ n <= view[e].room
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![e] = n]
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ view' = [view EXCEPT ![e] = NOREAD]
    /\ UNCHANGED drawn

Discard(e) ==
    /\ view[e] # NOREAD
    /\ view[e].version # version
    /\ view' = [view EXCEPT ![e] = NOREAD]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<drawn, held, version>>

Draw(e) ==
    /\ held[e] > 0
    /\ drawn' = [drawn EXCEPT ![e] = @ + held[e]]
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![e] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, view>>

Repay(e, n) ==
    /\ n > 0
    /\ n <= drawn[e]
    /\ drawn' = [drawn EXCEPT ![e] = @ - n]
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<held, view>>

Next ==
    \/ \E e \in Engines : Read(e) \/ Discard(e) \/ Draw(e)
    \/ \E e \in Engines, n \in 1..Ceiling : Reserve(e, n) \/ Repay(e, n)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

WithinCollateralCeiling == Exposure <= Ceiling

\* Every commit and every repayment advances the register, so the run is
\* cut off once the register has been turned MaxVersion times.
VersionBound == version <= MaxVersion
====

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Engines = {rtgs, netting}
    Ceiling = 2
    MaxVersion = 3
    NOREAD = NOREAD

INVARIANT WithinCollateralCeiling

CONSTRAINT VersionBound
nl:
A clearing bank runs two settlement engines that operate independently of each other: the real-time gross engine and the end-of-cycle netting engine. They draw intraday liquidity from one shared pool that the central bank has collateralised to a fixed ceiling. The ceiling is a hard limit on aggregate exposure — the bank's own drawings plus anything it has committed to draw must never exceed it.

Because the two engines do not coordinate, the shared pool exposes a single compare-and-swap register. An engine that wants liquidity first reads the register, which gives it two things: the register's current version, and the headroom left under the ceiling at that instant. The engine then works from what it read, not from a fresh look at the pool; that is the point of the read.

Committing is where the compare-and-swap happens. An engine may commit a reservation for an amount only if the register's version still equals the version it read, and only if the amount fits inside the headroom it read. A successful commit sets that engine's reservation aside and advances the register's version, which immediately makes the other engine's outstanding read worthless. An engine whose read has been overtaken throws it away and reads again. An engine holds at most one read and at most one reservation at a time.

A reservation is turned into an actual drawing when the engine settles the payments it reserved for. Repaying reduces an engine's drawing and advances the register's version, because headroom has changed.

The full set of actions is: Read, in which an engine with no read outstanding takes the register's version and the headroom currently left under the ceiling; Reserve, in which an engine commits a reservation for an amount that fits the headroom it read, provided the register's version still matches what it read, advancing the version; Discard, in which an engine whose read has been overtaken by a version change throws it away; Draw, in which an engine turns its reservation into an actual drawing; and Repay, in which an engine repays part of its drawing, advancing the register's version.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The liquidity drawn by the two engines, counted together with the amounts they have reserved and not yet drawn, never exceeds the collateralised ceiling on the shared pool.
