---- MODULE W4Od2m9p4t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Robots, Aisles, Occupancy, MaxEpoch, NOPERMIT

\* inside: robots physically in each aisle; permit: the entry permit a robot
\* is carrying; era: the aisle's floor-plan epoch; shut: aisles closed.
VARIABLES inside, permit, era, shut

vars == <<inside, permit, era, shut>>

Permits == [aisle: Aisles, era: 0..MaxEpoch]

TypeOK ==
    /\ inside \in [Aisles -> SUBSET Robots]
    /\ permit \in [Robots -> Permits \cup {NOPERMIT}]
    /\ era \in [Aisles -> 0..MaxEpoch]
    /\ shut \subseteq Aisles

Init ==
    /\ inside = [a \in Aisles |-> {}]
    /\ permit = [r \in Robots |-> NOPERMIT]
    /\ era = [a \in Aisles |-> 0]
    /\ shut = {}

Somewhere(r) == \E a \in Aisles : r \in inside[a]

\* An outstanding permit counts against the aisle from the moment it issues.
Booked(a) ==
    Cardinality(inside[a]) +
    Cardinality({r \in Robots : permit[r] # NOPERMIT
                                /\ permit[r].aisle = a
                                /\ permit[r].era = era[a]})

Issue(r, a) ==
    /\ a \notin shut
    /\ permit[r] = NOPERMIT
    /\ ~Somewhere(r)
    /\ Booked(a) < Occupancy
    /\ permit' = [permit EXCEPT ![r] = [aisle |-> a, era |-> era[a]]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inside, era, shut>>

\* A closed aisle does not stop a robot that already holds a valid permit.
Enter(r) ==
    /\ permit[r] # NOPERMIT
    /\ ~Somewhere(r)
    /\ era[permit[r].aisle] = permit[r].era
    /\ inside' = [inside EXCEPT ![permit[r].aisle] = @ \cup {r}]
    /\ permit' = [permit EXCEPT ![r] = NOPERMIT]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<era, shut>>

Void(r) ==
    /\ permit[r] # NOPERMIT
    /\ \/ era[permit[r].aisle] # permit[r].era
       \/ Somewhere(r)
    /\ permit' = [permit EXCEPT ![r] = NOPERMIT]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inside, era, shut>>

Leave(r, a) ==
    /\ r \in inside[a]
    /\ inside' = [inside EXCEPT ![a] = @ \ {r}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<permit, era, shut>>

Reconfigure(a) ==
    /\ inside[a] = {}
    /\ era[a] < MaxEpoch
    /\ era' = [era EXCEPT ![a] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inside, permit, shut>>

Close(a) == /\ a \notin shut
            /\ shut' = shut \cup {a}
            /\ UNCHANGED <<inside, permit, era>>

Open(a) == /\ a \in shut
           /\ shut' = shut \ {a}
           /\ UNCHANGED <<inside, permit, era>>

\* The supervisor skips the permit queue, never the occupancy figure.
Override(r, a) ==
    /\ a \notin shut
    /\ ~Somewhere(r)
    /\ Booked(a) < Occupancy
    /\ inside' = [inside EXCEPT ![a] = @ \cup {r}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<permit, era, shut>>

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Robots, a \in Aisles :
        Issue(r, a) \/ Leave(r, a) \/ Override(r, a)
    \/ \E r \in Robots : Enter(r) \/ Void(r)
    \/ \E a \in Aisles : Reconfigure(a) \/ Close(a) \/ Open(a)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
        /\ \A r \in Robots : SF_vars(Enter(r)) /\ SF_vars(Void(r))

WithinAisleOccupancy == \A a \in Aisles : Booked(a) <= Occupancy

NoPermitIsHeldForever ==
    \A r \in Robots : (permit[r] # NOPERMIT) ~> (permit[r] = NOPERMIT)
====

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Robots = {bot1, bot2}
    Aisles = {aisleA, aisleB}
    Occupancy = 1
    MaxEpoch = 1
    NOPERMIT = NOPERMIT

INVARIANT WithinAisleOccupancy

PROPERTY NoPermitIsHeldForever
nl:
A warehouse robot fleet moves pallets through picking aisles. An aisle takes only so many robots at once before they cannot pass each other, and that occupancy figure is a physical property of the aisle, not a tuning knob.

Robots do not drive into an aisle on their own initiative. The traffic manager issues an entry permit naming the aisle, and the robot drives in on that permit. Because a permit that has been issued is a robot that is going to be in the aisle, the manager counts outstanding permits against the aisle's occupancy from the moment it issues them, alongside the robots already inside. A robot holds at most one permit and is issued one only while it is not already in an aisle.

The floor plan is reconfigured under an epoch number as racking is moved, an aisle is re-striped, or a bay is turned around. Every reconfiguration of an aisle advances that aisle's epoch, and an aisle is only reconfigured while it is empty. A permit records the epoch of the aisle it was issued for; once the aisle's epoch advances, that permit describes a floor plan that no longer exists and is void. A permit is also void if the robot has meanwhile been put into an aisle by other means. A robot drives in only on a permit whose epoch still matches its aisle, and it leaves when its pick is done.

Aisles can be closed for maintenance. While an aisle is closed the manager issues no permits for it, but a robot already holding a valid permit may still drive in — a robot stopped in the mouth of an aisle is worse than a robot in it.

The shift supervisor has a privileged override and can put a robot straight into an open aisle with no permit at all, which is how a jam gets cleared without waiting for the traffic manager. What the supervisor cannot do is put a robot into an aisle that is already at its occupancy figure once the outstanding permits are counted, because the robots physically will not fit.

The full set of actions is: Issue, in which the traffic manager issues an entry permit for an open aisle to a robot that is outside and unpermitted, stamped with the aisle's epoch, provided the robots inside plus the permits outstanding leave room; Enter, in which a robot whose permit still carries its aisle's epoch drives in, consuming the permit; Void, in which a permit whose epoch has been superseded, or whose robot is already inside an aisle, is torn up; Leave, in which a robot inside an aisle drives out; Reconfigure, in which an empty aisle's floor plan changes and its epoch advances; Close and Open, in which an aisle is taken out of and put back into service; and Override, in which the supervisor puts a robot directly into an open aisle that still has room once inside robots and outstanding permits are counted.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every aisle, the robots inside it, counted together with the permits still outstanding at that aisle's current epoch, never exceed the aisle's occupancy figure.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: No robot is left holding a permit forever — every permit issued is eventually either driven in on or torn up.

---- MODULE W4Od1m8p4t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Controllers, Runways, WakeLimit, NONE

\* fieldLock: the coarse lock over the whole airport.
\* rwLock: the fine per-runway lock. prep: the clearance a controller has
\* prepared but not yet issued. rolling: aircraft currently on the runway.
VARIABLES fieldLock, rwLock, prep, rolling

vars == <<fieldLock, rwLock, prep, rolling>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ fieldLock \in Controllers \cup {NONE}
    /\ rwLock \in [Runways -> Controllers \cup {NONE}]
    /\ prep \in [Controllers -> Runways \cup {NONE}]
    /\ rolling \in [Runways -> 0..WakeLimit]

Init ==
    /\ fieldLock = NONE
    /\ rwLock = [rw \in Runways |-> NONE]
    /\ prep = [c \in Controllers |-> NONE]
    /\ rolling = [rw \in Runways |-> 0]

\* A prepared clearance is a departure that is going to be rolling.
Booked(rw) ==
    rolling[rw] + Cardinality({c \in Controllers : prep[c] = rw})

TakeField(c) ==
    /\ fieldLock = NONE
    /\ prep[c] = NONE
    /\ fieldLock' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED <<rwLock, prep, rolling>>

TakeRunway(c, rw) ==
    /\ fieldLock = c
    /\ rwLock[rw] = NONE
    /\ rwLock' = [rwLock EXCEPT ![rw] = c]
    /\ fieldLock' = NONE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<prep, rolling>>

DropField(c) ==
    /\ fieldLock = c
    /\ fieldLock' = NONE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<rwLock, prep, rolling>>

\* Only the runway's lock holder may prepare against that runway's room.
Prepare(c, rw) ==
    /\ rwLock[rw] = c
    /\ prep[c] = NONE
    /\ Booked(rw) < WakeLimit
    /\ prep' = [prep EXCEPT ![c] = rw]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fieldLock, rwLock, rolling>>

Issue(c) ==
    /\ prep[c] # NONE
    /\ rwLock[prep[c]] = c
    /\ rolling' = [rolling EXCEPT ![prep[c]] = @ + 1]
    /\ rwLock' = [rwLock EXCEPT ![prep[c]] = NONE]
    /\ prep' = [prep EXCEPT ![c] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED fieldLock

Airborne(rw) ==
    /\ rolling[rw] > 0
    /\ rolling' = [rolling EXCEPT ![rw] = @ - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fieldLock, rwLock, prep>>

DropRunway(c, rw) ==
    /\ rwLock[rw] = c
    /\ prep[c] = NONE
    /\ rwLock' = [rwLock EXCEPT ![rw] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fieldLock, prep, rolling>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : TakeField(c) \/ DropField(c) \/ Issue(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers, rw \in Runways :
        TakeRunway(c, rw) \/ Prepare(c, rw) \/ DropRunway(c, rw)
    \/ \E rw \in Runways : Airborne(rw)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

WithinWakeLimit == \A rw \in Runways : Booked(rw) <= WakeLimit
====

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Controllers = {ctlNorth, ctlSouth}
    Runways = {rwy09L, rwy27R}
    WakeLimit = 2
    NONE = NONE

INVARIANT WithinWakeLimit
nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator limits how many departures may be rolling on any one runway at the same time. The figure comes from wake-turbulence separation and is not negotiable: once that many aircraft are rolling, no further departure may be cleared onto that runway until one of them is airborne.

Clearances are written by controllers, and controllers reach a runway through two levels of lock. A controller must first take the field lock, which covers the whole airport, and only while holding it may it take the lock on one runway. Taking a runway's lock releases the field lock in the same step, so the coarse lock is held only long enough to choose a runway and other controllers can keep working.

Holding a runway's lock is what lets a controller prepare a departure clearance for it. A clearance that has been prepared but not yet acted on is a departure that is going to be rolling, so the allocator counts prepared clearances against the runway's limit alongside the aircraft already rolling. A controller holds at most one prepared clearance and only prepares while the aircraft rolling plus the clearances prepared leave room under the limit.

Controllers are slow but they do not fail. A controller that has taken a runway lock and prepared a clearance will get round to issuing it, but it may sit on that lock for a long time — coordinating with the tower, waiting on a wake check — and nothing takes the lock away from it. Issuing the clearance puts the aircraft onto the runway rolling, consumes the prepared clearance, and releases the runway lock. An aircraft that gets airborne frees its place on the runway. A controller that has taken the field lock, or a runway lock, and decided against a departure simply gives it back.

The full set of actions is: TakeField, in which a controller with no clearance prepared takes the free field lock; TakeRunway, in which a controller holding the field lock takes a free runway lock and releases the field lock in the same step; DropField, in which a controller gives the field lock back without choosing a runway; Prepare, in which a controller holding a runway lock prepares a departure clearance for it, provided the aircraft rolling plus the clearances prepared leave room under the limit; Issue, in which a controller's prepared clearance puts an aircraft onto its runway rolling and releases that runway's lock; Airborne, in which a rolling aircraft leaves the runway; and DropRunway, in which a controller with nothing prepared gives a runway lock back.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every runway, the aircraft rolling on it counted together with the departure clearances prepared for it never exceeds that runway's wake-separation limit.

---- MODULE W4Od13m7p1t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Machines, MaxPrice, Turnovers, NOREAD

\* price: the published schedule value; peak: the highest ever published.
\* reg: the compare-and-swap register. held: the read a machine is carrying.
\* up: a crashed machine acts no further and says nothing.
VARIABLES price, peak, reg, held, up

vars == <<price, peak, reg, held, up>>

Reads == [saw: 0..MaxPrice, reg: 0..Turnovers]

TypeOK ==
    /\ price \in 0..MaxPrice
    /\ peak \in 0..MaxPrice
    /\ reg \in 0..Turnovers
    /\ held \in [Machines -> Reads \cup {NOREAD}]
    /\ up \in [Machines -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
    /\ price = 0
    /\ peak = 0
    /\ reg = 0
    /\ held = [m \in Machines |-> NOREAD]
    /\ up = [m \in Machines |-> TRUE]

Read(m) ==
    /\ up[m]
    /\ held[m] = NOREAD
    /\ price < MaxPrice
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![m] = [saw |-> price, reg |-> reg]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<price, peak, reg, up>>

\* The new price is computed from what was read, so the register check is
\* the only thing standing between a stale read and a lost revision.
Write(m) ==
    /\ up[m]
    /\ held[m] # NOREAD
    /\ held[m].reg = reg
    /\ reg < Turnovers
    /\ price' = held[m].saw + 1
    /\ peak' = IF held[m].saw + 1 > peak THEN held[m].saw + 1 ELSE peak
    /\ reg' = reg + 1
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![m] = NOREAD]
    /\ UNCHANGED up

Reap(m) ==
    /\ held[m] # NOREAD
    /\ \/ held[m].reg # reg
       \/ reg >= Turnovers
       \/ ~up[m]
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![m] = NOREAD]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<price, peak, reg, up>>

Crash(m) ==
    /\ \A k \in Machines : up[k]
    /\ up' = [up EXCEPT ![m] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<price, peak, reg, held>>

Rejoin(m) ==
    /\ ~up[m]
    /\ up' = [up EXCEPT ![m] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<price, peak, reg, held>>

Next ==
    \E m \in Machines : Read(m) \/ Write(m) \/ Reap(m) \/ Crash(m) \/ Rejoin(m)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
        /\ \A m \in Machines : SF_vars(Write(m)) /\ SF_vars(Reap(m))

ScheduleNeverFallsBack == peak <= price

NoReadIsHeldForever ==
    \A m \in Machines : (held[m] # NOREAD) ~> (held[m] = NOREAD)
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Machines = {vm101, vm102}
    MaxPrice = 3
    Turnovers = 3
    NOREAD = NOREAD

INVARIANT ScheduleNeverFallsBack

PROPERTY NoReadIsHeldForever
nl:
A vending machine network keeps one shared price schedule for a product line. Machines revise it as costs move, and a revision is a read-modify-write: a machine reads the price now published, works out the next price up from what it read, and writes that back as the new published price. Two machines revising at once is how a revision gets lost — the second one writes a price computed from a schedule that has already moved.

The schedule sits behind a compare-and-swap register. Reading gives a machine two things: the price as published, and the register's current value. Writing back succeeds only if the register still holds the value the machine read; a successful write publishes the new price and turns the register over, which makes any other machine's outstanding read worthless. A machine whose read has been overtaken throws it away and reads again. A machine holds at most one read at a time.

The network also keeps a high-water mark: the highest price ever published on this schedule. It is what the operations team audits against, because a schedule that has gone backwards means a revision was computed from stale data and somebody's price increase was silently undone.

Machines can crash silently. A crashed machine stops reading and stops writing and gives no notice; a read it was holding is simply reaped by the network so the register does not stay pinned behind a machine that is not coming back on its own. A crashed machine can be power-cycled by the route driver and rejoins. At most one machine is down at a time. The register is turned over only a fixed number of times per pricing day; once it has been, outstanding reads are reaped rather than written back.

The full set of actions is: Read, in which a machine that is up and holding no read takes the published price and the register's current value; Write, in which a machine that is up writes back one above the price it read, provided the register still holds what it read and the day's turnover budget is not spent, publishing the new price, raising the high-water mark if it is higher, and turning the register over; Reap, in which an outstanding read is thrown away because the register has moved on, because the day's turnover budget is spent, or because the machine holding it has crashed; Crash, in which a machine that is up silently stops while every other machine is still up; and Rejoin, in which the crashed machine is power-cycled and comes back.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The published price is never below the highest price ever published on the schedule, so no revision is ever lost by being overwritten with a price computed from an older read.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: No machine is left holding a read forever — every read taken is eventually either written back or reaped.

---- MODULE W4Od2m6p2t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Robots, Bays, Pallets, LeaseFull, NONE

\* dock: pallets stacked at inbound; carried: pallets riding on each robot;
\* racked: pallets in each bay. lease/countdown: the bay lease and its timer.
VARIABLES dock, carried, racked, lease, countdown

vars == <<dock, carried, racked, lease, countdown>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ dock \in 0..Pallets
    /\ carried \in [Robots -> 0..Pallets]
    /\ racked \in [Bays -> 0..Pallets]
    /\ lease \in [Bays -> Robots \cup {NONE}]
    /\ countdown \in [Bays -> 0..LeaseFull]

Init ==
    /\ dock = Pallets
    /\ carried = [r \in Robots |-> 0]
    /\ racked = [b \in Bays |-> 0]
    /\ lease = [b \in Bays |-> NONE]
    /\ countdown = [b \in Bays |-> 0]

Total(f, S) ==
    LET add[T \in SUBSET S] ==
        IF T = {} THEN 0
        ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in T : TRUE IN f[x] + add[T \ {x}]
    IN add[S]

Pick(r, n) ==
    /\ n <= dock
    /\ dock' = dock - n
    /\ carried' = [carried EXCEPT ![r] = @ + n]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<racked, lease, countdown>>

Claim(r, b) ==
    /\ lease[b] = NONE
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![b] = r]
    /\ countdown' = [countdown EXCEPT ![b] = LeaseFull]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<dock, carried, racked>>

Stow(r, b, n) ==
    /\ lease[b] = r
    /\ n <= carried[r]
    /\ carried' = [carried EXCEPT ![r] = @ - n]
    /\ racked' = [racked EXCEPT ![b] = @ + n]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<dock, lease, countdown>>

Retrieve(r, b, n) ==
    /\ lease[b] = r
    /\ n <= racked[b]
    /\ racked' = [racked EXCEPT ![b] = @ - n]
    /\ carried' = [carried EXCEPT ![r] = @ + n]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<dock, lease, countdown>>

Tick(b) ==
    /\ lease[b] # NONE
    /\ countdown[b] > 0
    /\ countdown' = [countdown EXCEPT ![b] = @ - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<dock, carried, racked, lease>>

\* A lapse frees the bay and takes nothing off the robot.
Lapse(b) ==
    /\ lease[b] # NONE
    /\ countdown[b] = 0
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![b] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<dock, carried, racked, countdown>>

Release(r, b) ==
    /\ lease[b] = r
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![b] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<dock, carried, racked, countdown>>

Return(r, n) ==
    /\ n <= carried[r]
    /\ carried' = [carried EXCEPT ![r] = @ - n]
    /\ dock' = dock + n
    /\ UNCHANGED <<racked, lease, countdown>>

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Robots, n \in 1..Pallets : Pick(r, n) \/ Return(r, n)
    \/ \E r \in Robots, b \in Bays : Claim(r, b) \/ Release(r, b)
    \/ \E r \in Robots, b \in Bays, n \in 1..Pallets :
        Stow(r, b, n) \/ Retrieve(r, b, n)
    \/ \E b \in Bays : Tick(b) \/ Lapse(b)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

PalletsAreConserved ==
    dock + Total(carried, Robots) + Total(racked, Bays) = Pallets
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Robots = {agv1, agv2}
    Bays = {bayA, bayB}
    Pallets = 2
    LeaseFull = 1
    NONE = NONE

INVARIANT PalletsAreConserved
nl:
A warehouse robot fleet moves pallets between the inbound dock and the racking. Pallets are physical goods and the stock controller reconciles them at the end of every shift: at any instant every pallet in the building is either stacked at the dock, riding on a robot, or racked in one of the storage bays. None appear and none disappear.

A robot may only put pallets into a bay, or take pallets out of one, while it holds that bay's lease. Leases are used rather than permanent assignments because robots are slow: a robot that has claimed a bay may take a long time over the transfer — it is re-planning its route, its lift is cycling, the aisle ahead is congested — and if bays were assigned permanently one slow robot would sterilise a bay for the rest of the shift. A lease therefore runs on a countdown that ticks down while the lease is held, and when the countdown reaches zero the lease lapses and the bay is free for somebody else.

Robots are slow but they do not fail, and a lapse takes nothing away from them. A robot whose lease lapses while it is still carrying pallets keeps every pallet it was carrying; it simply cannot put them into that bay any more until it claims a lease again. Pallets on a robot are still pallets. A robot can also hand pallets it is carrying back to the dock at any time, which needs no lease, and it can give a lease back voluntarily when it is finished.

The full set of actions is: Pick, in which a robot takes pallets from the dock stack onto itself; Claim, in which a robot takes the lease on a free bay and starts its countdown at full; Stow, in which a robot holding a bay's lease moves pallets it is carrying into that bay; Retrieve, in which a robot holding a bay's lease takes pallets out of that bay onto itself; Tick, in which a running lease countdown decreases by one; Lapse, in which a lease whose countdown has reached zero is released by the warehouse; Release, in which a robot gives a bay's lease back voluntarily; and Return, in which a robot hands pallets it is carrying back to the dock stack.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The pallets stacked at the inbound dock, plus the pallets riding on the robots, plus the pallets racked in the storage bays, always add up to exactly the number of pallets the building holds.

---- MODULE W4Od2m9p5t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Robots, Trailers, MaxEpoch, OPEN, NONE

\* plan: the dock-plan epoch. decision: the intent a slow robot is carrying.
\* register: the yard's record of who sealed each trailer.
\* onboard: each robot's own log of the trailers it sealed.
VARIABLES plan, decision, register, onboard

vars == <<plan, decision, register, onboard>>

Decisions == [trailer: Trailers, plan: 0..MaxEpoch]

TypeOK ==
    /\ plan \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ decision \in [Robots -> Decisions \cup {NONE}]
    /\ register \in [Trailers -> Robots \cup {OPEN}]
    /\ onboard \in [Robots -> SUBSET Trailers]

Init ==
    /\ plan = 0
    /\ decision = [r \in Robots |-> NONE]
    /\ register = [t \in Trailers |-> OPEN]
    /\ onboard = [r \in Robots |-> {}]

Decide(r, t) ==
    /\ decision[r] = NONE
    /\ register[t] = OPEN
    /\ decision' = [decision EXCEPT ![r] = [trailer |-> t, plan |-> plan]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<plan, register, onboard>>

\* Two checks before the seal goes on: the plan is current, and the trailer
\* is still open on the register.
Seal(r) ==
    /\ decision[r] # NONE
    /\ decision[r].plan = plan
    /\ register[decision[r].trailer] = OPEN
    /\ register' = [register EXCEPT ![decision[r].trailer] = r]
    /\ onboard' = [onboard EXCEPT ![r] = @ \cup {decision[r].trailer}]
    /\ decision' = [decision EXCEPT ![r] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED plan

Abandon(r) ==
    /\ decision[r] # NONE
    /\ \/ decision[r].plan # plan
       \/ register[decision[r].trailer] # OPEN
    /\ decision' = [decision EXCEPT ![r] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<plan, register, onboard>>

Reconfigure ==
    /\ plan < MaxEpoch
    /\ plan' = plan + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<decision, register, onboard>>

Rest ==
    /\ \A t \in Trailers : register[t] # OPEN
    /\ \A r \in Robots : decision[r] = NONE
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Robots, t \in Trailers : Decide(r, t)
    \/ \E r \in Robots : Seal(r) \/ Abandon(r)
    \/ Reconfigure \/ Rest

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
        /\ \A r \in Robots : SF_vars(Seal(r)) /\ SF_vars(Abandon(r))

OnboardLogsMatchTheRegister ==
    \A r \in Robots : \A t \in onboard[r] : register[t] = r

NoDecisionOutstandingForever ==
    \A r \in Robots : (decision[r] # NONE) ~> (decision[r] = NONE)
====

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Robots = {agvRed, agvBlue}
    Trailers = {trlA, trlB}
    MaxEpoch = 2
    OPEN = OPEN
    NONE = NONE

INVARIANT OnboardLogsMatchTheRegister

PROPERTY NoDecisionOutstandingForever
nl:
A warehouse robot fleet closes out outbound trailers. Sealing a trailer is irreversible: the robot fits the numbered customs seal, the paperwork is cut against that seal number, and the trailer cannot be reopened on the yard. Fitting a second seal to a trailer that already has one is a customs discrepancy that has to be resolved with the carrier, so a trailer is sealed once or not at all.

The yard register is the authority on what has been sealed: for each trailer it records the robot that sealed it, or that it is still open. Every robot also keeps its own on-board log of the trailers it has sealed, which is what the fleet's end-of-day reconciliation reads.

The dock plan is reconfigured under an epoch number as doors are reassigned and trailers are re-spotted. Advancing the epoch changes which trailer is at which door, so a decision made under the old plan no longer points at the trailer the robot thought it did.

Robots are slow but they do not fail. A robot decides to seal a particular open trailer, recording the epoch it decided under, and then takes its time getting there — it is finishing another move, its seal magazine is being reloaded, it is waiting for a door to clear. By the time it arrives the dock plan may have been reconfigured, or another robot may have sealed that trailer already. So the robot checks twice before it fits the seal: the epoch it decided under must still be the current one, and the yard register must still show the trailer open. If either check fails the decision is abandoned unacted. A robot holds at most one decision at a time.

The full set of actions is: Decide, in which a robot with no decision outstanding picks a trailer the register shows as open and records a decision stamped with the current dock-plan epoch; Seal, in which a robot whose decision still carries the current epoch and whose trailer the register still shows open fits the seal, is recorded in the yard register as that trailer's sealer, and writes the trailer into its own log; Abandon, in which a decision whose epoch has been superseded, or whose trailer has already been sealed, is dropped unacted; Reconfigure, in which the dock plan advances to the next epoch; and Rest, in which the fleet simply waits once every trailer is sealed and no robot has a decision outstanding.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every trailer a robot has written into its own log is a trailer the yard register records as sealed by that same robot, so no trailer is ever sealed twice.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: No robot is left with a decision outstanding forever — every decision a robot records is eventually either acted on by sealing or abandoned.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od10m7p0t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Trains, StampLimit, NONE

\* assigned: the train the crossover register names; stamp: the register's
\* compare-and-swap value, turned over on every change of assignment.
\* ticket: the stamp each train was handed. fouling: who is on the crossover.
VARIABLES assigned, stamp, ticket, fouling

vars == <<assigned, stamp, ticket, fouling>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ assigned \in Trains \cup {NONE}
    /\ stamp \in Nat
    /\ ticket \in [Trains -> Nat \cup {NONE}]
    /\ fouling \in [Trains -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
    /\ assigned = NONE
    /\ stamp = 0
    /\ ticket = [t \in Trains |-> NONE]
    /\ fouling = [t \in Trains |-> FALSE]

Clear == \A t \in Trains : ~fouling[t]

Grant(t) ==
    /\ assigned = NONE
    /\ ~fouling[t]
    /\ ticket[t] = NONE
    /\ assigned' = t
    /\ stamp' = stamp + 1
    /\ ticket' = [ticket EXCEPT ![t] = stamp + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED fouling

Enter(t) ==
    /\ ~fouling[t]
    /\ assigned = t
    /\ ticket[t] = stamp
    /\ fouling' = [fouling EXCEPT ![t] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<assigned, stamp, ticket>>

Leave(t) ==
    /\ fouling[t]
    /\ fouling' = [fouling EXCEPT ![t] = FALSE]
    /\ assigned' = NONE
    /\ ticket' = [ticket EXCEPT ![t] = NONE]
    /\ stamp' = stamp + 1

Void(t) ==
    /\ ticket[t] # NONE
    /\ ~fouling[t]
    /\ \/ ticket[t] # stamp
       \/ assigned # t
    /\ ticket' = [ticket EXCEPT ![t] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<assigned, stamp, fouling>>

\* The controller does not queue behind the grant sequence, but will not
\* reassign a junction a train is standing on.
Override(t) ==
    /\ Clear
    /\ assigned' = t
    /\ stamp' = stamp + 1
    /\ ticket' = [k \in Trains |-> IF k = t THEN stamp + 1 ELSE NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED fouling

Next == \E t \in Trains : Grant(t) \/ Enter(t) \/ Leave(t)
                          \/ Void(t) \/ Override(t)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

FoulingTrainOwnsTheCrossover ==
    \A t \in Trains : fouling[t] => (assigned = t /\ ticket[t] = stamp)

\* Every assignment change turns the stamp over, so the run is cut off once
\* the register has been turned StampLimit times.
StampBound == stamp <= StampLimit
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Trains = {trA, trB}
    StampLimit = 4
    NONE = NONE

INVARIANT FoulingTrainOwnsTheCrossover

CONSTRAINT StampBound
nl:
A subway line has a flat crossover where two routes intersect. The crossover is the critical resource: one train may be on it at a time, and a second train on it while the first is still fouling the junction is a collision, not a delay.

Ownership of the crossover is held in a single compare-and-swap register on the interlocking. The register holds the train it is currently assigned to, together with a stamp that is turned over on every change of assignment — every grant, every release, and every intervention by the signaller. A train that is granted the crossover is handed a ticket carrying the stamp as it stood at that grant, and the train may only move onto the crossover while its ticket still matches the register's stamp and the register still names it. A ticket that no longer matches is torn up and the train asks again.

The line controller has a privileged override. When a service recovery is running, the controller can reassign the crossover to a chosen train without waiting for the current holder to give it up, turning the stamp over as it does so and issuing that train a fresh ticket. That is the whole point of the override: it does not queue behind the normal grant sequence. What the controller will not do is reassign a crossover that a train is physically standing on. An intervention is only made once the junction is clear, because the stamp turnover invalidates the standing train's ticket without moving the train, and a train fouling a junction that has been handed to somebody else is exactly the collision the interlocking exists to prevent.

A train that has finished crossing moves off, which releases the register, tears up its ticket, and turns the stamp over again.

The full set of actions is: Grant, in which the interlocking assigns the unassigned crossover to a train that is not on it, turning the stamp over and issuing that train a ticket carrying the new stamp; Enter, in which a train whose ticket still matches the register's stamp, and which the register still names, moves onto the crossover; Clear, in which a train on the crossover moves off, releasing the register, tearing up its ticket, and turning the stamp over; Void, in which a train tears up a ticket that no longer matches the register; and Override, in which the controller reassigns the crossover to a chosen train while no train is on it, turning the stamp over and issuing that train a fresh ticket.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any train standing on the crossover is the train the register names, holding a ticket that still matches the register's stamp, so two trains are never on the crossover together.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od18m6p3t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Guests, Slots, MaxGen, NONE

\* gen: each slot's generation, advanced on every change of hands.
\* holder: the guest a slot is leased to. key: the single-use key a guest
\* carries, recording the generation it was cut at. logged: entries made.
VARIABLES gen, holder, key, logged

vars == <<gen, holder, key, logged>>

Keys == [slot: Slots, gen: 0..MaxGen]

TypeOK ==
    /\ gen \in [Slots -> 0..MaxGen]
    /\ holder \in [Slots -> Guests \cup {NONE}]
    /\ key \in [Guests -> Keys \cup {NONE}]
    /\ logged \subseteq Guests

Init ==
    /\ gen = [s \in Slots |-> 0]
    /\ holder = [s \in Slots |-> NONE]
    /\ key = [g \in Guests |-> NONE]
    /\ logged = {}

Grant(g, s) ==
    /\ holder[s] = NONE
    /\ key[g] = NONE
    /\ gen[s] < MaxGen
    /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![s] = g]
    /\ gen' = [gen EXCEPT ![s] = @ + 1]
    /\ key' = [key EXCEPT ![g] = [slot |-> s, gen |-> gen[s] + 1]]
    /\ UNCHANGED logged

Lapse(s) ==
    /\ holder[s] # NONE
    /\ gen[s] < MaxGen
    /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![s] = NONE]
    /\ gen' = [gen EXCEPT ![s] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<key, logged>>

Enter(g) ==
    /\ key[g] # NONE
    /\ gen[key[g].slot] = key[g].gen
    /\ holder[key[g].slot] = g
    /\ gen[key[g].slot] < MaxGen
    /\ gen' = [gen EXCEPT ![key[g].slot] = @ + 1]
    /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![key[g].slot] = NONE]
    /\ key' = [key EXCEPT ![g] = NONE]
    /\ logged' = logged \cup {g}

Discard(g) ==
    /\ key[g] # NONE
    /\ \/ gen[key[g].slot] # key[g].gen
       \/ holder[key[g].slot] # g
       \/ gen[key[g].slot] >= MaxGen
    /\ key' = [key EXCEPT ![g] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<gen, holder, logged>>

\* The homeowner skips the lease queue, never the generation bump.
Override(g, s) ==
    /\ key[g] = NONE
    /\ gen[s] < MaxGen
    /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![s] = g]
    /\ gen' = [gen EXCEPT ![s] = @ + 1]
    /\ key' = [key EXCEPT ![g] = [slot |-> s, gen |-> gen[s] + 1]]
    /\ UNCHANGED logged

Rest ==
    /\ \A s \in Slots : gen[s] = MaxGen
    /\ \A g \in Guests : key[g] = NONE
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E g \in Guests, s \in Slots : Grant(g, s) \/ Override(g, s)
    \/ \E g \in Guests : Enter(g) \/ Discard(g)
    \/ \E s \in Slots : Lapse(s)
    \/ Rest

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
        /\ \A g \in Guests : SF_vars(Enter(g)) /\ SF_vars(Discard(g))

LiveKeyMatchesTheHolder ==
    \A g \in Guests :
        (key[g] # NONE /\ key[g].gen = gen[key[g].slot])
            => holder[key[g].slot] = g

NoKeyIsCarriedForever ==
    \A g \in Guests : (key[g] # NONE) ~> (key[g] = NONE)
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Guests = {cleaner, contractor}
    Slots = {slot1, slot2}
    MaxGen = 2
    NONE = NONE

INVARIANT LiveKeyMatchesTheHolder

PROPERTY NoKeyIsCarriedForever
nl:
A smart-home door lock network hands out guest access through a small fixed set of keypad code slots. A slot holds one guest's code at a time; giving the same slot to two guests would mean the cleaner's code opens the door for the contractor, which is exactly the confusion the slot numbering exists to prevent.

A slot is not assigned permanently. It is leased: the hub records a slot as held by a guest and issues that guest a key. Every slot carries a generation number that advances whenever the slot changes hands — on every grant, on every lapse, on every use, and on every intervention by the homeowner — and the key a guest receives records the generation the slot was on when the key was cut. That generation is what tells a live key from one the hub has already moved past.

Guest keys are single use. A guest whose key still carries its slot's current generation, and whose slot the hub still records as theirs, uses the key to get in; the entry is logged, the key is spent, the slot is released and its generation advances. A guest whose key no longer matches — the lease lapsed, the slot was reassigned, or the slot has run out of generations for the day — throws the key away. A guest holds at most one key. Leases also lapse on their own when a guest never turns up.

The homeowner has a privileged override and can hand a slot to a chosen guest straight from the app, without waiting for the current lease to lapse. What the override does not skip is the generation: reassigning a slot advances its generation like any other change, because that is what makes the previous holder's key stop working. Leaving the generation alone would leave two live keys on one slot.

The full set of actions is: Grant, in which the hub leases a free slot to a guest holding no key, advancing the slot's generation and cutting a key that records it; Lapse, in which a slot's lease expires with nobody having used it, releasing the slot and advancing its generation; Enter, in which a guest whose key still matches its slot's generation and holder uses it, logging the entry, spending the key, releasing the slot and advancing its generation; Discard, in which a guest throws away a key whose generation or holder no longer matches, or whose slot has no generations left for the day; Override, in which the homeowner reassigns a slot to a chosen guest, advancing the slot's generation and cutting that guest a fresh key; and Rest, in which the hub simply waits once every slot has run out of generations and no guest is holding a key.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever a guest holds a key whose generation is still the current generation of its slot, the hub records that very guest as the slot's holder, so a slot is never live for two guests at once.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: No guest is left holding a key forever — every key cut is eventually either used to enter or thrown away.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od18m2p5t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS LockCount, MinBatch

\* A lock is numbered, and its number is the fuse charge it draws, so the
\* charges are distinct and the audit is not just a headcount.
Locks == 1..LockCount
Charge(l) == l
Stocked == (LockCount * (LockCount + 1)) \div 2

\* phase: where the two-phase round stands. answer: each lock's part in the
\* round. blown: locks whose fuse is gone. stock: charges left in the hub.
\* limit: how many locks the hub will put in one batch, retuned at runtime.
VARIABLES phase, answer, blown, stock, limit

vars == <<phase, answer, blown, stock, limit>>

Answers == {"unasked", "yes", "no", "done"}

TypeOK ==
    /\ phase \in {"idle", "voting", "committing"}
    /\ answer \in [Locks -> Answers]
    /\ blown \subseteq Locks
    /\ stock \in 0..Stocked
    /\ limit \in MinBatch..LockCount

Init ==
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ answer = [l \in Locks |-> "unasked"]
    /\ blown = {}
    /\ stock = Stocked
    /\ limit = MinBatch

Drawn(S) ==
    LET add[T \in SUBSET Locks] ==
        IF T = {} THEN 0
        ELSE LET l == CHOOSE x \in T : TRUE IN Charge(l) + add[T \ {l}]
    IN add[S]

Batch == {l \in Locks : answer[l] # "unasked"}

Open ==
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ phase' = "voting"
    /\ answer' = [l \in Locks |-> "unasked"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<blown, stock, limit>>

Ask(l, a) ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ answer[l] = "unasked"
    /\ l \notin blown
    /\ Cardinality(Batch) < limit
    /\ answer' = [answer EXCEPT ![l] = a]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, blown, stock, limit>>

Abort ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ \E l \in Locks : answer[l] = "no"
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ answer' = [l \in Locks |-> "unasked"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<blown, stock, limit>>

Commit ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ Batch # {}
    /\ \A l \in Batch : answer[l] = "yes"
    /\ phase' = "committing"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<answer, blown, stock, limit>>

\* A lock already blown is never in a batch, so no charge is drawn twice.
Blow(l) ==
    /\ phase = "committing"
    /\ answer[l] = "yes"
    /\ l \notin blown
    /\ Charge(l) <= stock
    /\ blown' = blown \cup {l}
    /\ stock' = stock - Charge(l)
    /\ answer' = [answer EXCEPT ![l] = "done"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, limit>>

Close ==
    /\ phase = "committing"
    /\ \A l \in Locks : answer[l] # "yes"
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ answer' = [l \in Locks |-> "unasked"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<blown, stock, limit>>

Retune ==
    /\ \E n \in MinBatch..LockCount : limit' = n
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, answer, blown, stock>>

Next ==
    \/ Open \/ Abort \/ Commit \/ Close \/ Retune
    \/ \E l \in Locks : Blow(l) \/ (\E a \in {"yes", "no"} : Ask(l, a))

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

FuseStockIsAccountedFor == stock + Drawn(blown) = Stocked
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    LockCount = 3
    MinBatch = 1

INVARIANT FuseStockIsAccountedFor
nl:
A smart-home door lock network is rolling out a security fix that permanently blows a one-time fuse inside each lock, closing off the factory recovery path for good. Blowing the fuse is irreversible in the strongest sense available to a consumer device: the silicon is altered, there is no undo, and blowing it a second time is not merely wasteful but would draw a second fuse charge out of a hub that has only so many.

The hub holds a stock of fuse charges, and each lock model draws a different, known amount of that stock when its fuse is blown. The stock is what the installer audits: charges that are still in the hub, plus the charges consumed by the locks that have been blown, must always account for exactly what the hub started with.

The rollout runs as a two-phase commit. The hub opens a round and puts the question to a batch of locks: each lock asked in the round answers yes if it is ready to blow its fuse or no if it is not. Only when every lock in the round has answered yes does the hub move the round into its commit phase; a single no aborts the round outright and nobody blows anything. In the commit phase the locks that answered yes blow their fuses one at a time, each drawing its own charge from the hub's stock, and a lock that has blown is marked done and is never asked again in a later round. A lock already blown is never put into a batch.

How many locks the hub will put into one round is retuned at runtime — a bigger batch when the house is quiet and the mesh is idle, a smaller one when the radio is busy or the hub is on battery — and the limit in force is what caps the batch as it is being assembled. A round whose locks have all blown is closed and the hub goes idle.

The full set of actions is: Open, in which the idle hub opens a new round with nobody yet asked; Ask, in which the hub puts the question to an unasked, unblown lock and receives a yes or a no, permitted only while the batch is below the current limit; Abort, in which a round in which some lock answered no is closed without anything being blown; Commit, in which a round whose asked locks all answered yes moves into its commit phase; Blow, in which a lock that answered yes in a committed round blows its fuse, draws its charge from the hub's stock, and is marked done; Close, in which a committed round with nothing left to blow returns the hub to idle; and Retune, in which the hub sets the batch limit to any supported value.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The fuse charges remaining in the hub's stock, plus the charges drawn by the locks that have been blown, always add up to exactly the stock the hub started with, so no lock's fuse is ever blown twice.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od18m6p1t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Phones, MaxDelay, NONE

\* delay: the shared auto-relock setting. lease: who may compose and write.
\* mesh: changes in flight, picked up in no particular order.
\* confirmed: the value the hub last acknowledged to each phone.
VARIABLES delay, lease, mesh, confirmed

vars == <<delay, lease, mesh, confirmed>>

Changes == [by: Phones, saw: 0..MaxDelay]

TypeOK ==
    /\ delay \in 0..MaxDelay
    /\ lease \in Phones \cup {NONE}
    /\ mesh \subseteq Changes
    /\ confirmed \in [Phones -> (0..MaxDelay) \cup {NONE}]

Init ==
    /\ delay = 0
    /\ lease = NONE
    /\ mesh = {}
    /\ confirmed = [p \in Phones |-> NONE]

Outstanding(p) == \E c \in mesh : c.by = p

Take(p) ==
    /\ lease = NONE
    /\ ~Outstanding(p)
    /\ lease' = p
    /\ UNCHANGED <<delay, mesh, confirmed>>

Compose(p) ==
    /\ lease = p
    /\ ~Outstanding(p)
    /\ delay < MaxDelay
    /\ mesh' = mesh \cup {[by |-> p, saw |-> delay]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<delay, lease, confirmed>>

\* The hub writes what was sent; the lease check is the whole mechanism.
Apply(c) ==
    /\ c \in mesh
    /\ lease = c.by
    /\ delay' = c.saw + 1
    /\ confirmed' = [confirmed EXCEPT ![c.by] = c.saw + 1]
    /\ mesh' = mesh \ {c}
    /\ lease' = NONE

Bin(c) ==
    /\ c \in mesh
    /\ lease # c.by
    /\ mesh' = mesh \ {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<delay, lease, confirmed>>

Expire ==
    /\ lease # NONE
    /\ lease' = NONE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<delay, mesh, confirmed>>

Next ==
    \/ \E p \in Phones : Take(p) \/ Compose(p)
    \/ \E c \in Changes : Apply(c) \/ Bin(c)
    \/ Expire

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
        /\ \A c \in Changes : SF_vars(Apply(c)) /\ SF_vars(Bin(c))

SettingNeverStepsBack ==
    \A p \in Phones : confirmed[p] # NONE => delay >= confirmed[p]

NoChangeStaysOnTheMesh ==
    \A c \in Changes : (c \in mesh) ~> (c \notin mesh)
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Phones = {phoneA, phoneB}
    MaxDelay = 2
    NONE = NONE

INVARIANT SettingNeverStepsBack

PROPERTY NoChangeStaysOnTheMesh
nl:
A smart-home door lock network keeps one shared setting that every lock in the house obeys: the auto-relock delay. Household members change it from their phones, and a change is a read-modify-write — the phone reads the delay as it stands, works out the next step up, and sends that value back to the hub. Two phones doing that at once is how somebody's change quietly disappears.

The hub arbitrates with a write lease. Only the phone currently holding the lease may compose a change, and only a change from the phone that holds the lease is applied. Leases expire on their own, so a phone that goes out of range or gets locked in a pocket does not freeze the setting for everybody else.

Changes reach the hub over the house mesh, which does not preserve order. A composed change sits on the mesh and is picked up in whatever order the radio manages, so a change composed under an earlier lease can easily be picked up after a change composed under a later one. A phone has at most one change outstanding.

The hub does not re-derive the value when a change lands — it writes what the phone sent. What it checks is the lease: a change is applied only if the phone that composed it is still the lease holder. That check is the whole safety mechanism, because a phone whose lease has gone composed its value against a delay the hub has since moved past, and writing it would step the setting backwards. A change from a phone that no longer holds the lease is binned unapplied. Applying a change also acknowledges it back to the composing phone, which remembers the value the hub confirmed, and releases the lease.

The full set of actions is: Take, in which a phone with nothing outstanding takes the free write lease; Compose, in which the lease-holding phone reads the delay, works out the next step up, and puts the resulting change onto the mesh; Apply, in which a change whose composer still holds the lease is written to the setting, acknowledged back to that phone, and the lease released; Bin, in which a change whose composer no longer holds the lease is discarded unapplied; and Expire, in which an outstanding lease lapses on its own.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The auto-relock delay is never below a value the hub has acknowledged to a phone, so no confirmed change is ever undone by a change composed against an older reading.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: No change stays on the mesh forever — every change a phone composes is eventually taken off it, either applied or binned.
